literature_review.synthesis:
The open problem asks whether strict equilibrium strategies for continuous-time portfolio choice under rank-dependent utility (RDU)—defined via conditional quantiles and a probability weighting function—can be genuinely non-deterministic (progressively measurable and not a deterministic function of time) in an incomplete Brownian market with constant coefficients. The source paper (Wei–Xia–Zhao, 2024) develops a detailed theory for deterministic strict equilibrium strategies (DSES): in the time-invariant weighting case, equilibria (when they exist) are essentially unique and characterized by an autonomous singular ODE for the future integrated variance \,\(\Pi(t)=\int_t^T\|\pi(s)^\top\sigma\|^2ds\); in the time-varying weighting case (mainly \(\gamma\le 0\)), non-zero DSES correspond to positive solutions of a nonlinear singular ODE (with possible multiplicity), and the paper provides forward-shooting methods and an “optimal equilibrium” selection criterion among DSES. The authors explicitly note that they do not know whether any non-deterministic equilibrium exists.

Among the provided forward citations, the only analyzed citing work studies a different time-inconsistent preference (random risk aversion aggregated via certainty equivalents) and likewise focuses on deterministic equilibria characterized by an ODE. While it reinforces that spike-variation equilibrium conditions often collapse to low-dimensional ODEs under homotheticity and deterministic coefficients, it does not treat quantile-based RDU functionals nor the key difficulty here: the dependence of \(J(t,x;\pi)\) on the conditional law of \(X_T^\pi\) given \(\mathcal F_t\), which becomes substantially more complex for stochastic \(\pi\) in incomplete markets.

Overall, based on the source paper and the limited forward-citation evidence supplied, there is currently no known existence or nonexistence theorem for non-deterministic strict equilibrium strategies under RDU in the stated setting. Progress appears to require new techniques to handle conditional quantiles under progressively measurable controls—potentially via conditional distribution dynamics, mean-field/measure-valued control formulations, or identifying structural conditions under which any SES must collapse to a deterministic feedback (or proving counterexamples by constructing stochastic equilibria).

sources.title: Equilibrium Investment with Random Risk Aversion:(Non-) uniqueness, Optimality, and Comparative Statics
sources.theorem_or_result: In a Black–Scholes market with deterministic coefficients and an objective given by an average of CRRA certainty equivalents over a random risk aversion parameter \(R\), the paper characterizes all deterministic equilibrium strategies \(\bar\pi(t)=(\sigma^\top(t))^{-1}a(t)\) by the condition \(a(t)=h(v(t))\lambda(t)\), where \(v(t)=\int_t^T |a(s)|^2ds\), \(\lambda(t)=\sigma(t)^{-1}\mu(t)\), and \(h(x)=\frac{\tilde\E[e^{-\frac12 R x}]}{\tilde\E[R e^{-\frac12 R x}]}\). Equivalently \(v\) solves the ODE \(v'(t)=-h(v(t))^2|\lambda(t)|^2\), \(v(T)=0\), yielding closed-form existence/uniqueness/multiplicity results for deterministic equilibria depending on \(\tilde\E[R]\) and \(H(\infty)=\int_0^\infty h(x)^{-2}dx\) (Theorem 3.2), and an optimal-selection criterion among multiple deterministic equilibria when \(\tilde\E[R]=\infty\) (Theorem 4.4).
sources.connection: The open problem asks whether there exist non-deterministic (progressively measurable, genuinely random) strict equilibrium strategies for a *rank-dependent utility* (RDU) functional defined via conditional quantiles and probability weighting \(w(t,\cdot)\). This citing paper instead studies a different time-inconsistent preference: an average of CRRA certainty equivalents over a random risk aversion distribution (RRA). It restricts attention to deterministic candidate equilibria \(\Pi_d\) and provides a complete characterization within that class; it does not analyze existence/nonexistence of non-deterministic equilibria, nor does it treat RDU/quantile-based objectives. Methodologically, it uses the same spike-variation equilibrium notion and derives equilibrium conditions/ODEs for deterministic equilibria, which is only indirectly relevant as a technique template for equilibrium characterization, not as a resolution of the RDU non-deterministic equilibrium existence question.

title: Determine the price of strategyproofness for social welfare with three resources
background_latex:
Consider the multi-resource allocation model with a set of agents \(N=\{1,2,\dots,n\}\) and a set of divisible resources \(R=\{1,2,\dots,m\}\), where each resource has total supply normalized to \(1\).

Each agent \(i\in N\) has a normalized demand vector \(d_i=(d_{i1},\dots,d_{im})\in(0,1]^m\) with \(\max_{r\in R} d_{ir}=1\). The dominant resource of agent \(i\) is any \(r_i^*\in\arg\max_{r\in R} d_{ir}\).

An allocation is a matrix \(A=(A_{ir})_{i\in N,r\in R}\) where \(A_{ir}\ge 0\) is the fraction of resource \(r\) allocated to agent \(i\). Feasibility requires \(\sum_{i\in N} A_{ir}\le 1\) for all \(r\in R\).

Agents have Leontief preferences: the utility of agent \(i\) under allocation \(A\) is
\[
 u_i(A_i)=\max\{y\ge 0: A_{ir}\ge y\, d_{ir}\ \text{for all } r\in R\},
\]
where \(A_i=(A_{i1},\dots,A_{im})\).

A mechanism is a function \(f\) mapping every demand profile \((d_1,\dots,d_n)\) to a feasible allocation \(f(d_1,\dots,d_n)\).

Define the following properties for a mechanism \(f\):

1) Share incentive (SI): for every instance, for all \(i\), \(u_i(f_i)\ge 1/n\).

2) Envy freeness (EF): for every instance, for all \(i,j\), \(u_i(f_i)\ge u_i(f_j)\).

3) Pareto optimality (PO): for every instance, there is no feasible allocation \(A'\) with \(u_i(A'_i)\ge u_i(f_i)\) for all \(i\) and \(u_{i_0}(A'_{i_0})>u_{i_0}(f_{i_0})\) for some \(i_0\).

4) Strategyproofness (SP): for every instance and agent \(i\), misreporting \(d'_i\) cannot increase \(u_i\), i.e., if \(I\) is the true profile and \(I'\) differs only in agent \(i\)'s report, then \(u_i(f_i(I))\ge u_i(f_i(I'))\).

The utilitarian social welfare of an allocation is \(\mathrm{SW}(A)=\sum_{i\in N} u_i(A_i)\).

Given an instance \(I=(d_1,\dots,d_n)\), let \(\mathrm{OPT}_{\mathrm{fair}}(I)\) denote the maximum social welfare over all feasible allocations that satisfy SI and EF:
\[
\mathrm{OPT}_{\mathrm{fair}}(I)=\max\{\mathrm{SW}(A): A \text{ feasible and satisfies SI and EF}\}.
\]

For a mechanism \(f\), its fair-ratio for social welfare is
\[
\mathrm{FR}_{\mathrm{SW}}(f)=\sup_I \frac{\mathrm{OPT}_{\mathrm{fair}}(I)}{\mathrm{SW}(f(I))}.
\]

For a fixed number of resources \(m\), the price of strategyproofness (for social welfare) is the best achievable fair-ratio among mechanisms satisfying SI, EF, PO, and SP:
\[
\mathrm{PoSP}_{\mathrm{SW}}(m)=\inf_{f\ \text{satisfies SI,EF,PO,SP}} \mathrm{FR}_{\mathrm{SW}}(f).
\]

The setting of interest here is \(m=3\) resources.
problem_definition_latex:
Determine the exact value of \(\mathrm{PoSP}_{\mathrm{SW}}(3)\), where
\[
\mathrm{PoSP}_{\mathrm{SW}}(3)=\inf_{f\ \text{satisfies SI,EF,PO,SP}}\ \sup_I \frac{\mathrm{OPT}_{\mathrm{fair}}(I)}{\mathrm{SW}(f(I))}
\]
and \(\mathrm{OPT}_{\mathrm{fair}}(I)=\max\{\mathrm{SW}(A): A \text{ feasible and satisfies SI and EF}\}\) for the 3-resource Leontief multi-resource allocation problem described above.

Equivalently, close (or determine) the gap between the known bounds
\[
2 \le \mathrm{PoSP}_{\mathrm{SW}}(3) \le 3.
\]

title: Characterize DDPM low-dimensional adaptivity under Wasserstein or total variation metrics
background_latex:
Let \(p_{\mathrm{data}}\) be a probability distribution on \(\mathbb{R}^d\) with support \(\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{data}}\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d\). Consider the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck forward diffusion \((X_t)_{t\in[0,T]}\) defined by
\[
\mathrm{d}X_t = -X_t\,\mathrm{d}t + \sqrt{2}\,\mathrm{d}W_t,\qquad X_0\sim p_{\mathrm{data}},
\]
where \((W_t)\) is standard Brownian motion in \(\mathbb{R}^d\). Let \(q_t\) denote the law of \(X_t\). The (Stein) score of \(q_t\) is \(s_t(x)=\nabla \log q_t(x)\).

The ideal reverse-time SDE associated with this forward process is
\[
\mathrm{d}Y_t = \bigl(Y_t + 2 s_{T-t}(Y_t)\bigr)\,\mathrm{d}t + \sqrt{2}\,\mathrm{d}B_t,\qquad Y_0\sim q_T,
\]
where \((B_t)\) is an independent standard Brownian motion, and in the ideal case \(Y_{T-t}\) has the same law as \(X_t\).

A denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) sampler operates in discrete time with a grid \(0=t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_N<T\). Starting from \(Y_{t_0}\sim \mathcal{N}(0,I_d)\), it iteratively updates \(Y_{t_n}\mapsto Y_{t_{n+1}}\) using a particular combination of the current iterate, an estimate \(\hat s_{T-t_n}\) of the score \(s_{T-t_n}\), and fresh Gaussian noise (the precise coefficients are chosen so that this discrete-time procedure equals the time-discretization of a certain semi-linear reverse SDE).

literature_review.synthesis:
In Huang--Wei--Chen (2026 revision of arXiv:2410.18784), DDPM is shown to be nearly optimally adaptive to intrinsic dimension \(k\) when discrepancy is measured in KL: with a two-phase grid and early stopping \(\delta\), one can achieve \(\mathrm{KL}(q_\delta\|p_{\mathrm{out}})\lesssim \varepsilon^2\) using \(N=\tilde O(k/\varepsilon^2)\) steps (Corollary 1). The paper explicitly leaves open whether analogous \(k\)-adaptive guarantees hold for stronger or different metrics such as total variation and Wasserstein distances.

The total-variation side has since been resolved in a sharp, intrinsic-dimension-adaptive way by "Low-dimensional adaptation of diffusion models: Convergence in total variation", which proves \(\mathrm{TV}\) bounds of order \(\tilde O(k/T)\) (plus score-error terms) for DDPM with the original Ho et al. coefficients, under the same type of metric-entropy/covering-number intrinsic dimension and bounded-support assumptions used to motivate \(k\) in Huang--Wei--Chen. Closely related works develop complementary TV theories: Li--Yan's \(O(d/T)\) theory gives a baseline \(d\)-dependent TV rate under minimal assumptions and shows how modified coefficients can yield \(k\)-dependent TV rates; probability-flow ODE analyses establish \(\tilde O(k/T)\) TV convergence for DDIM-like samplers under similar intrinsic-dimension assumptions; and rectified-flow perspectives recover \(\tilde O(k/N)\) TV control for DDPM-equivalent stochastic samplers via time change.

For Wasserstein metrics, the landscape is less complete for unconditional DDPM under the covering-number intrinsic dimension \(k\). The strongest partial progress comes from end-to-end statistical/generalization analyses that bound \(W_p\) (including \(W_2\)) with rates governed by intrinsic Wasserstein dimension notions, and from algorithmic results giving dimension-free \(W_2\) (and sometimes TV) guarantees under compact-support-plus-Gaussian-convolution and Lipschitz score assumptions. There are also \(W_2\) adaptivity results in guided diffusion (Doob matching) under a low-dimensional subspace model. A remaining gap is a direct, nonasymptotic \(W_2(q_\delta,p_{\mathrm{out}})\) (or \(W_2(p_{\mathrm{data}},p_{\mathrm{out}})\)) bound for the vanilla DDPM discretization in the Huang--Wei--Chen OU/metric-entropy setting, with iteration complexity scaling as \(\tilde O(k\,\mathrm{poly}(1/\varepsilon))\) and without imposing strong smoothness/log-concavity. Promising directions include combining the posterior-covariance/metric-entropy control ideas (used for KL and TV) with Wasserstein stability estimates for SDE discretizations, potentially via coupling/contractivity localized to the \(k\)-dimensional typical set, or by proving intrinsic-dimension versions of transportation inequalities that convert KL/TV control into \(W_2\) under low-dimensional structure.

sources.title: Low-dimensional adaptation of diffusion models: Convergence in total variation
sources.theorem_or_result: The paper proves total-variation convergence guarantees for DDIM and DDPM that adapt to intrinsic dimension. Under a covering-number intrinsic dimension assumption (Assumption 1) and bounded support (Assumption 2), and assuming accurate scores (or controlled score error), it shows for DDPM with original Ho et al. coefficients that \(\mathrm{TV}(p_{X_1},p_{Y_1})\lesssim k\log^3 T/T + \varepsilon_{\mathrm{score}}\sqrt{\log T}\) (Theorem 2), and for DDIM with original Song et al. coefficients that \(\mathrm{TV}(p_{X_1},p_{Y_1})\lesssim k\log^3 T/T + (\varepsilon_{\mathrm{score}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{Jacobi},1}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{Jacobi},2}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{Hess}})\sqrt{\log T}\) (Theorem 1). In particular, with exact scores these imply iteration complexity \(\tilde O(k/\varepsilon)\) to reach TV error \(\varepsilon\).
sources.connection: The open problem asks for conditions under which DDPM achieves low-dimensional adaptivity when discrepancy is measured in TV or Wasserstein rather than KL. This paper directly addresses the TV part: it establishes TV convergence rates and \(\tilde O(k/\varepsilon)\) iteration complexity for both DDPM and DDIM under minimal distributional assumptions (covering-number intrinsic dimension and bounded support), without smoothness/log-concavity. It also analyzes coefficient choices and provides a one-step lower bound showing near-necessity of the original DDIM/DDPM coefficients for dimension-adaptive TV control. However, it does not provide Wasserstein (e.g., \(W_2\)) guarantees, so it does not fully resolve the open problem as stated (which includes Wasserstein).

sources.title: Generalization Properties of Score-matching Diffusion Models for Intrinsically Low-dimensional Data
sources.theorem_or_result: Theorem 13 (in the citing paper): for a target distribution \(\mu\) on \(\mathbb{R}^D\) with finite \(q\)-moment \(M_q(\mu)<\infty\) (Assumption 1) and OU-type forward diffusion with bounded time-scaling \(0<\underline\beta\le \beta_t\le \overline\beta\) (Assumption 2), fix \(1\le p<q\) and any \(d>d^{\star}_{p,q}(\mu)\) (the paper’s \((p,q)\)-Wasserstein dimension). With specific choices of diffusion horizon \(T\gtrsim \frac{1}{2\underline\beta}\bigl(\frac{2p(1+q-p)}{d(q-p)}\log n + \log(D+M_2(\mu)^2)\bigr)\), reverse early-stopping \(\delta_0=n^{-2/(pd)}\), step size parameter \(\kappa\asymp n^{-\frac{2p(1+q-p)}{d(q-p)}}\) (hence \(N\lesssim \kappa^{-1}(\log(1/\delta_0)+T)\)), truncation radius \(R\asymp n^{\frac{1}{d(q-p)}}\), and a ReLU score network class \(\mathcal S\), the DDPM/exponential-integrator sampler output distribution \(\mathrm{TR}(\widehat Q_{T-\delta_0}(\widehat s_n))\) satisfies \[\mathbb E\,W_p\bigl(\mu,\mathrm{TR}(\widehat Q_{T-\delta_0}(\widehat s_n))\bigr)\ \lesssim\ n^{-1/d}\,\mathrm{poly\text{-}log}(n).\] The same rate holds for the Monte-Carlo-trained score \(\widehat s^{\mathrm{mc}}_n\) under a lower bound on per-time Monte Carlo sample sizes \(m_i\).
sources.connection: The open problem asks for intrinsic-dimension-adaptive DDPM convergence guarantees under metrics like \(W_2\) or TV (beyond KL), with iteration complexity scaling with intrinsic dimension \(k\) rather than ambient \(d\). This paper directly provides Wasserstein-\(p\) (hence in particular \(W_2\) when \(p=2\)) risk bounds for score-matching diffusion models trained from finite samples, where the convergence exponent depends on an intrinsic dimension parameter \(d^{\star}_{p,q}(\mu)\) (defined via covering numbers) rather than ambient dimension. It also specifies a nonuniform discretization/partition and yields an explicit bound on the number of reverse steps \(N\lesssim \kappa^{-1}(\log(1/\delta_0)+T)\), with \(\kappa\) chosen as a negative power of \(n\) involving \(d\) (any upper bound on \(d^{\star}_{p,q}(\mu)\)), thus giving an iteration complexity that is polynomial in \(n\) with exponent depending on intrinsic dimension. However, it does not treat total variation guarantees, and its intrinsic dimension notion \(d^{\star}_{p,q}(\mu)\) is not exactly the \(k\) from the original open problem (covering number of support at fixed scale), though it is closely related and often equals manifold dimension in regular cases. Thus it constitutes strong partial progress for Wasserstein metrics but not a complete characterization for TV/fully matching the original \(k\)-parameter statement.

sources.title: O (d/T) convergence theory for diffusion probabilistic models under minimal assumptions
sources.theorem_or_result:
For the discrete-time DDPM sampler 
\[Y_{t-1}=\alpha_t^{-1/2}(Y_t+\eta_t s_t(Y_t)+\sigma_t Z_t),\quad Z_t\sim\mathcal N(0,I_d),\]
under Assumption 1 (finite first moment of \(p_{\mathrm{data}}\)) and \(\ell_2\)-accurate score estimates with averaged error \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{score}}^2=\tfrac1T\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbb E\|s_t(X_t)-s_t^*(X_t)\|_2^2\), the paper proves:
- (Theorem 1) with coefficients \(\eta_t=\sigma_t^2=1-\alpha_t\),
\[\mathrm{TV}(p_{X_1},p_{Y_1})\le c\,\frac{d\log^3 T}{T}+c\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{score}}\sqrt{\log T}.\]
- (Theorem 3) with a modified coefficient design \(\eta_t=1-\alpha_t\), \(\sigma_t^2=\frac{(1-\alpha_t)(\alpha_t-\bar\alpha_t)}{1-\bar\alpha_t}\), and intrinsic dimension \(k\) defined via metric entropy \(\log N_\varepsilon(\mathrm{supp}(p_{\mathrm{data}}))\lesssim k\log T\),
\[\mathrm{TV}(p_{X_1},p_{Y_1})\le c\,\frac{k\log^3 T}{T}+c\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{score}}\sqrt{\log T}.\]
sources.connection: The open problem asks for low-dimensional adaptivity guarantees for DDPM under metrics other than KL, specifically total variation and Wasserstein. This paper directly addresses the TV part: it establishes dimension-dependent \(O(d/T)\) TV convergence under minimal moment assumptions and improves to \(O(k/T)\) TV convergence when the data support has intrinsic dimension \(k\) (metric entropy) and the DDPM coefficients are carefully chosen. However, it does not provide Wasserstein (e.g., \(W_2\)) convergence/adaptivity results; it explicitly lists extending to Wasserstein as future work. Also, its forward process is the discrete-time DDPM forward chain rather than the continuous-time Ornstein--Uhlenbeck SDE in the problem statement, though it is closely related via discretization.

sources.title: Adaptivity and convergence of probability flow ODEs in diffusion generative models
sources.theorem_or_result:
For the discrete-time probability flow ODE (DDIM) sampler with the DDIM coefficient choice \(\eta_t=\eta_t^\star:=1-\alpha_t-\sqrt{(1-\alpha_t)(\bar\alpha_t-\bar\alpha_{t-1})}\) and under bounded-support and intrinsic-dimension (metric entropy) assumptions on \(\mathcal X=\mathrm{supp}(p_{\mathrm{data}})\), the paper proves
\[
\mathrm{TV}(p_{X_1},p_{Y_1})\le c\,\frac{(k+\log d)\,\log^3 T}{T}+c\,(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{score}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{Jacobi}})\,\log T,
\]
where \(k\) is the intrinsic dimension defined via \(\log N_\varepsilon(\mathcal X)\lesssim k\log T\), and \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{score}},\varepsilon_{\mathrm{Jacobi}}\) are average score and Jacobian estimation errors along the forward marginals.
sources.connection: The open problem asks for low-dimensional adaptivity guarantees for diffusion samplers under metrics other than KL, specifically TV and Wasserstein \(W_2\), for DDPM-type samplers. This paper directly addresses the TV part but for the deterministic probability flow ODE (a DDIM-type sampler), proving an \(\tilde O(k/T)\) TV convergence rate (plus score/Jacobian error terms) that depends on intrinsic dimension \(k\) rather than ambient \(d\). It does not provide a Wasserstein \(W_2\) adaptivity result, and it is not a DDPM (stochastic reverse SDE) analysis; the authors explicitly list extending to Wasserstein as future work. Thus it constitutes partial progress toward the broader characterization requested in the open problem.

sources.title: High-accuracy and dimension-free sampling with diffusions
sources.theorem_or_result: For targets of the form \(q=q_{\mathrm{pre}}\ast \mathcal N(0,\sigma^2 I_d)\) where \(q_{\mathrm{pre}}\) is supported in a radius-\(R\) ball (Assumption 1), the paper gives a diffusion-based sampler (collocation/Picard solver for the probability flow ODE using score estimates) that achieves high-accuracy convergence: with Lipschitz score estimates and sub-exponential score error, Algorithm 2 outputs \(\hat q\) with \(W_2(q,\hat q)\le \tilde O(\varepsilon\log^2(1/\varepsilon))\) using \(\tilde O((R/\sigma)^2\log^2(1/\varepsilon))\) score-oracle calls (Theorem 3.7 / Theorem G.1). Under an additional Lipschitzness assumption on the true score \(\nabla\log q\), a corrected version (Algorithm 3) achieves \(\mathrm{TV}(q,\hat q)\le \varepsilon\) in \(\tilde O((R/\sigma)^2)\) iterations (Corollary 3.9), with an explicit requirement on score error \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{sc}}\lesssim \tilde O(\varepsilon^{2/3} L^{1/2} d^{1/6}(R/\sigma)^{2/3})\).
sources.connection: The open problem asks for low-dimensional adaptivity of DDPM-type samplers under \(\mathrm{TV}\) or \(W_2\), i.e. iteration complexity scaling with intrinsic dimension \(k\) (covering number) rather than ambient \(d\). This paper provides convergence guarantees directly in \(W_2\) (Theorem 3.7) and \(\mathrm{TV}\) (Corollary 3.9), and its complexity is ‘dimension-free’ in the sense of not depending explicitly on \(d\), depending instead on a geometric parameter (support radius \(R\) of the pre-noise distribution) and noise level \(\sigma\). This is partial progress toward the open problem because it addresses the requested metrics and favorable dimension dependence, but it does not characterize adaptivity in terms of intrinsic dimension \(k\) (covering number/manifold dimension) for DDPM; the dependence is via \(R/\sigma\) and additional assumptions (compact support + Gaussian convolution, sub-exponential score error, and for TV an extra corrector step and Lipschitz true score). Thus it complements but does not resolve the specific \(k\)-adaptivity question for DDPM under \(\mathrm{TV}\)/\(W_2\).

sources.title: Inference-Time Alignment for Diffusion Models via Variationally Stable Doob's Matching
sources.theorem_or_result:
The paper proves non-asymptotic convergence guarantees for an inference-time guided diffusion sampler (a controllable reverse-time OU SDE discretized by an exponential integrator) in 2-Wasserstein distance, with rates adaptive to intrinsic dimension under a low-dimensional subspace assumption. In particular, under bounded-support and bounded-weight assumptions and an L2 reference-score error bound, Theorem 5.6 shows
\[\mathbb{E}\, W_2^2\bigl(q_0,(M\circ T_R)_\#\hat q_{T-T_0}\bigr)\le C\,\varepsilon\,\log^3(1/\varepsilon),\]
for suitable choices of terminal time \(T\), steps \(K\), step size \(h\), early stopping \(T_0\), truncation radius \(R\), reference score error \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{ref}}\), and sample size \(n\) used to estimate Doob guidance. Moreover, under Assumption 4 (data supported on a \(d^*\)-dimensional linear subspace), Theorem 5.9 gives guidance estimation error
\[\mathbb{E}\,\|\nabla\log \hat h_t-\nabla\log h_t^*\|_{L^2(p_{T-t})}^2\le C\,\sigma_{T-t}^{-8}\, n^{-2/(d^*+8)}\,\log^4 n,\]
and Corollary 5.10 yields the same Wasserstein convergence with sample complexity depending exponentially on \(d^*\) rather than ambient \(d\).
sources.connection: The open problem asks for low-dimensional adaptivity guarantees for DDPM-type samplers under metrics like total variation or Wasserstein (rather than KL), with iteration/sample complexity scaling with intrinsic dimension \(k\). This paper directly provides Wasserstein-2 convergence bounds for a diffusion sampler with an added guidance drift (Doob’s h-transform) and explicitly proves adaptivity to unknown low dimensionality (intrinsic dimension \(d^*\)) in the guidance estimation and end-to-end sampling error (Theorems 5.6, 5.9, Corollary 5.10). However, it does not analyze the standard unconditional DDPM sampler targeting \(p_{\mathrm{data}}\) itself; instead it studies inference-time alignment/tilting of a reference diffusion model to a target \(q_0\) via guidance, and its main end-to-end bound is in \(W_2\) (with an auxiliary KL decomposition). It also does not fully address total variation guarantees for the final output (though it derives a TV bound for the early-stopping distribution via Pinsker as a corollary). Thus it constitutes substantial partial progress toward the Wasserstein/TV adaptivity question, but not a complete resolution of the original open problem in full generality.

sources.title: Low-Dimensional Adaptation of Rectified Flow: A New Perspective through the Lens of Diffusion and Stochastic Localization
sources.theorem_or_result:
The paper proves total-variation convergence bounds for rectified flow (RF) and a stochastic RF sampler that are adaptive to intrinsic dimension. In particular, under a metric-entropy intrinsic-dimension condition (Assumption 4.1) and bounded support (Assumption 4.2), the stochastic RF sampler (equivalent to a DDPM under a time change) satisfies (Theorem 4.7)
\[
\mathrm{TV}(\mathrm{Law}(Y_{t_{N-1}}),\mathrm{Law}(X_{t_{N-1}})) \lesssim \frac{k\log^3 N}{N} + \varepsilon_s\sqrt{\log N},
\]
where \(k\) is the intrinsic dimension and \(\varepsilon_s\) is an average score-approximation error. For deterministic RF with a U-shaped time grid, Theorem 4.5 gives
\(\mathrm{TV}(p_{X_{t_{N-1}}},p_{Y_{t_{N-1}}})\lesssim (k\log^3(1/\delta))/N\) plus terms depending on drift/derivative approximation errors and \(\delta\).
sources.connection: The open problem asks for low-dimensional adaptivity guarantees for DDPM sampling under metrics like total variation or Wasserstein (rather than KL), with iteration complexity scaling with intrinsic dimension \(k\). This paper directly establishes \(k\)-adaptive total-variation bounds for RF and for a stochastic RF sampler (STOC-RF) and proves STOC-RF is equivalent to DDPM (OU/variance-schedule DDPM) via stochastic localization and a time change (Proposition 3.5). Consequently, it provides TV convergence rates of order \(\tilde O(k/N)\) (and hence \(\tilde O(k/\varepsilon)\) steps for TV error \(\varepsilon\) in the idealized/noiseless-estimation regime) for a DDPM-equivalent sampler, partially answering the open problem in the TV metric. However, it does not fully characterize DDPM adaptivity in \(W_2\) or TV for the exact OU reverse-SDE discretization in the generality of the open problem; the results are framed through RF/STOC-RF with specific schedules and approximation-error assumptions, and do not provide a Wasserstein adaptivity theorem.

title: Establish smoothing and gradient consistency for value functions with x-dependent constraints
background_latex:
Consider the bilevel optimization problem
\[
\min_{(x,y)\in X\times Y(x)} f(x,y) \quad \text{s.t.}\quad y\in \arg\min_{\bar y\in Y(x)} g(x,\bar y),
\]
where \(X\subseteq \mathbb{R}^n\) is a closed convex set, and the lower-level feasible set \(Y(x)\subseteq \mathbb{R}^m\) depends on \(x\). The functions \(f,g\) are (possibly nonsmooth) real-valued functions; the paper’s main body treats the fixed-set case \(Y(x)\equiv Y\) and focuses on the lower-level value function
\[
v(x):=\min_{y\in Y} g(x,y)
\]
(or analogously \(v(x):=\min_{y\in Y(x)} g(x,y)\) in the \(x\)-dependent case) and smooth approximation families \(\{v_\mu\}_{\mu>0}\) intended to satisfy:
1) (smoothing/approximation) \(v_\mu\) is continuously differentiable and \(v_\mu(x)\to v(x)\) as \((x,\mu)\to (\bar x,0)\), and
2) (gradient consistency) any cluster point of \(\nabla v_\mu(x)\) as \((x,\mu)\to (\bar x,0)\) lies in the Clarke subdifferential \(\partial v(\bar x)\).

In the \(x\)-dependent constraint setting, the relevant lower-level value function becomes
\[
v(x):=\min_{y\in Y(x)} g(x,y),
\]
and one seeks to construct a family \(\{v_\mu\}_{\mu>0}\) (potentially based on regularization/penalization of the lower-level problem and/or smoothing of \(g\) and of the set-valued mapping \(x\mapsto Y(x)\)) that is a smoothing family in the above sense and is gradient consistent.
problem_definition_latex:
Determine conditions and a concrete construction under which, for the \(x\)-dependent lower-level feasible set \(Y(x)\), the resulting smooth approximation \(\{v_\mu\}_{\mu>0}\) of the value function \(v(x)=\min_{y\in Y(x)} g(x,y)\) (obtained for example by a quadratic-regularization combined with penalization approach) is:
\[
\text{(i) a smoothing family: } v_\mu \in C^1 \text{ and } \lim_{(x,\mu)\to(\bar x,0)} v_\mu(x)=v(\bar x),
\]
and
\[
\text{(ii) gradient consistent at each } \bar x: \varnothing\neq \limsup_{(x,\mu)\to(\bar x,0)} \nabla v_\mu(x) \subseteq \partial v(\bar x).
\]
Here \(\partial v(\bar x)\) denotes the Clarke subdifferential of \(v\) at \(\bar x\), and
\[
\limsup_{(x,\mu)\to(\bar x,0)} \nabla v_\mu(x):=\left\{\xi:\exists x_k\to \bar x,\ \mu_k\downarrow 0\ \text{with }\nabla v_{\mu_k}(x_k)\to \xi\right\}.
\]

title: Equilibrium-equivalent reduction of zero-sum games to cone-leveled strategy games
background_latex:
A two-player zero-sum game is a triple \(G=(S,T,u)\), where \(S\subseteq X\) and \(T\subseteq Y\) are the strategy sets of players I and II, and \(u:S\times T\to\mathbb{R}\) is the payoff to player I.

In the setting considered here, \(X\) and \(Y\) are (reflexive) Banach spaces with continuous duals \(X^*\) and \(Y^*\). A bilinear pairing is denoted by \(\langle \cdot,\cdot\rangle\). A (closed convex) cone \(C\subseteq X\) has positive dual cone \(C^*:=\{w\in X^*: \langle w,x\rangle\ge 0\ \forall x\in C\}\), and similarly for a cone \(K\subseteq Y\).

A cone-leveled set is a subset \(S\subseteq X\) that can be written as
\[
S=\{x\in C: \langle \alpha,x\rangle\in H\},
\]
for some convex cone \(C\subseteq X\), some nonzero functional \(\alpha\in X^*\), and some nonempty set \(H\subseteq (0,\infty)\) (typically an interval). A basic cone-leveled set is the special case \(H=\{p\}\) (a single level). A base of a cone is a basic cone-leveled set \(\{x\in C: \langle \alpha,x\rangle=1\}\) with \(\alpha\in \mathrm{int}(C^*)\).

Two games \(G=(S,T,u)\) and \(G'=(S',T',u')\) are equilibrium-equivalent if they have the same set of Nash equilibria after an identification of strategies (e.g., via maps between \(S\) and \(S'\), \(T\) and \(T'\)) that preserves saddle-point inequalities, so that equilibria and game values correspond under the identification.

The paper establishes that games whose strategy sets are cone-leveled (in particular, bases of convex cones) and whose payoff is bilinear \(u(x,y)=\langle y,Ax\rangle\) can be analyzed/solved via associated conic linear programs and duality. This motivates asking which more general games can be reduced, without changing equilibrium structure, to this cone-leveled class.

literature_review.synthesis:
Dimou’s framework isolates a broad class of zero-sum games—those with cone-leveled strategy sets and bilinear payoff \,\(u(x,y)=\langle y,Ax\rangle\)—for which equilibria and values can be computed via associated conic linear programs, and conversely shows an “almost equivalence” between minimax and strong duality in reflexive Banach spaces. The open problem asks for a characterization of when an arbitrary zero-sum game \(G=(S,T,u)\) is equilibrium-equivalent (via strategy identifications preserving saddle inequalities) to such a cone-leveled bilinear game \(\widetilde G\), thereby enabling conic-programming machinery to solve the original game without changing its equilibrium structure.

The only forward-citing work provided here makes partial progress in a major subclass: semidefinite programming. It constructs, under verifiable constraint qualifications (strong optimality or strict unboundedness), an equilibrium-preserving reduction from an SDP pair to a zero-sum semidefinite game whose strategy sets are density matrices (bases of the PSD cone) and whose payoff is bilinear. This aligns closely with Dimou’s cone-base setting and demonstrates that, at least for SDPs, one can build explicit equivalence mappings that allow recovery of primal/dual solutions or certificates from game equilibria.

However, the general characterization problem remains open: beyond specific conic-programming-derived games (LP/SDP and variants), there is no known necessary-and-sufficient condition describing exactly which general Banach-space games admit an equilibrium-equivalent embedding into the cone-leveled bilinear class. Promising directions suggested by Dimou’s paper include identifying invariants of equilibrium structure preserved under positive-homogeneous rescalings and cone-base normalizations, and developing criteria that recognize when a game’s payoff and feasible strategy geometry can be represented (possibly after lifting) as linear images of cone slices (bases or cone-leveled sets), as in moment/SOS liftings for polynomial games.

sources.theorem_or_result:
Under a constraint qualification for an SDP pair \((P,D)\)—either (i) existence of strongly optimal primal-dual solutions (attainment and zero duality gap) or (ii) existence of a strictly unbounded direction—the paper constructs a modified zero-sum semidefinite game \(G_M\) (players’ strategies are density matrices with a block-diagonal form encoding \((X,y,t)\) plus an extra scalar \(u\)) with bilinear payoff \(p(\bar X,\bar Y)\) such that:
- \(\mathrm{val}(G_M)=0\) iff a strongly optimal primal-dual pair exists; and if \(\mathrm{val}(G_M)=0\), any optimal strategy of player 2 has \(t>0\) and yields strongly optimal SDP solutions \((X/t,\,y/t)\) (Theorem 3.6).
- If a strictly unbounded direction exists, then for any optimal strategy of player 1 one has \(t'=0\) and the strategy yields an unbounded direction certificate for \(P\) or \(D\) (Theorem 3.10).
Moreover, for rational input they give an explicit bound \(M\) (via KKT root/coordinate bounds) guaranteeing the reduction works in the bounded case (Corollary 4.3).
sources.connection: The open problem asks for necessary/sufficient conditions for when a general zero-sum game \((S,T,u)\) is equilibrium-equivalent to a cone-leveled, bilinear game \(\langle \tilde y,\tilde A\tilde x\rangle\). This paper provides such an equilibrium-preserving reduction in one important subclass: SDPs (a specific conic program over \(S_+^n\)) are reduced to a zero-sum semidefinite game whose strategy sets are density matrices (a base of the PSD cone, hence basic cone-leveled) and whose payoff is bilinear in the players’ matrix strategies. The reduction is shown to preserve optimal strategies/equilibria and to allow recovery of primal/dual SDP solutions or infeasibility/unboundedness certificates, but only under a stated constraint qualification (strong optimality or strict unboundedness). It does not characterize reductions for arbitrary Banach-space games \((S,T,u)\), nor for general cones beyond the semidefinite cone, though it suggests extension to conic games as future work.

title: Existence of interior discount factor where decreasing and increasing value trajectories coincide
background_latex:
Let $K=\{1,\dots,k\}$ be a finite state space and let $M$ be an irreducible stochastic matrix on $K$ with unique invariant distribution $\pi_M\in\Delta(K)$. In a Markovian persuasion game, the sender observes the current state $X_n\in K$ of the Markov chain in real time and sends a signal; the receiver chooses an action based on his posterior belief, yielding a stage payoff to the sender. For each discount factor $\delta\in[0,1)$ and prior $q\in\Delta(K)$, let $v_\delta(q)$ denote the sender's optimal expected $(1-\delta)$-normalized $\delta$-discounted payoff.

Let $e_\ell\in\Delta(K)$ denote the Dirac belief on state $\ell\in K$ (i.e., $e_\ell(\ell)=1$). Define two functions of the discount factor $\delta$:
\[
\Phi(\delta):=v_\delta(\pi_M),\qquad \Psi(\delta):=\sum_{\ell\in K} \pi_M(\ell)\, v_\delta(e_\ell).
\]
For irreducible $M$, the paper establishes that $\Phi$ is non-increasing in $\delta$ (when the prior is invariant) and that $\Psi$ is non-decreasing in $\delta$ (as a particular instance of an increasing weighted-average trajectory). Moreover, for each fixed $\delta$, concavity of $v_\delta(\cdot)$ implies $\Phi(\delta)\ge \Psi(\delta)$.

Define
\[
\delta_0:=\inf\{\delta\in[0,1):\Phi(\delta)=\Psi(\delta)\},
\]
with the convention that the set may be empty (equivalently, $\Phi(\delta)>\Psi(\delta)$ for all $\delta\in[0,1)$). The paper notes that if equality holds at some $\delta_0$, then both $\Phi$ and $\Psi$ must be constant on $[\delta_0,1)$; hence the qualitative possibility of an equality point $\delta_0\in(0,1)$ is a distinct regime from equality only at $\delta=1$ (in the limit) or no equality at all.
problem_definition_latex:
Determine whether there exists a Markovian persuasion game with finite state space $K$ and irreducible transition matrix $M$ such that the associated functions
\[
\Phi(\delta)=v_\delta(\pi_M),\qquad \Psi(\delta)=\sum_{\ell\in K} \pi_M(\ell)\, v_\delta(e_\ell)
\]
satisfy
\[
\Phi(\delta)>\Psi(\delta)\ \text{for all }\delta\in[0,\delta_0),\qquad \Phi(\delta)=\Psi(\delta)\ \text{for all }\delta\in[\delta_0,1)
\]
for some \emph{interior} point $\delta_0\in(0,1)$ (equivalently, whether equality can first occur strictly before $\delta=1$).

title: Decidability of feasible-set membership for robust-to-linear-dynamics linear programs
background_latex:
Consider discrete-time linear dynamics on \(\mathbb{R}^n\) given by \(x_{k+1}=Gx_k\), where \(G\in\mathbb{Q}^{n\times n}\) is a rational matrix. Let the constraint set be a (rational) polyhedron \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n: Ax\le b\}\), with \(A\in\mathbb{Q}^{m\times n\), \(b\in\mathbb{Q}^m\), and inequalities interpreted componentwise.

Define the set of \(P\)-invariant initial conditions under \(G\) by
\[
S := \bigcap_{k=0}^{\infty}\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n : G^k x \in P\} 
   = \bigcap_{k=0}^{\infty}\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n : A G^k x \le b\}.
\]
Equivalently, \(x\in S\) if and only if the entire forward orbit \(\{G^k x\}_{k\ge 0}\) stays in \(P\).

The associated decision problem (membership problem) takes as input \((A,b,G,z)\) with \(z\in\mathbb{Q}^n\) and asks whether \(z\in S\). This is the feasibility question underlying robust-to-linear-dynamics linear programs (R-LD-LPs), i.e., linear programs with the additional constraint that iterates under \(G\) remain in \(P\) forever.
problem_definition_latex:
Given rational data \(A\in\mathbb{Q}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{Q}^m\), \(G\in\mathbb{Q}^{n\times n}\), and \(z\in\mathbb{Q}^n\), decide whether
\[
z \in S := \bigcap_{k=0}^{\infty}\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n : A G^k x \le b\}.
\]
Equivalently, decide whether \(AG^k z\le b\) holds for all integers \(k\ge 0\).

literature_review.synthesis:
In the notation of Ahmadi–Günlük’s robust-to-dynamics optimization framework, the membership question asks whether a rational query point \(z\) satisfies the semi-infinite family of linear inequalities \(AG^k z\le b\) for all \(k\ge 0\), i.e., whether \(z\in S:=\bigcap_{k\ge0}G^{-k}P\). The source paper establishes that this feasible set \(S\) is closed, convex, and invariant, but can be non-polyhedral even for rational data (e.g., irrational rotations yielding a disk), and that membership is NP-hard (Theorem 2.1). It also identifies three “barriers” to finite convergence of the natural outer approximations \(S_r:=\bigcap_{k=0}^r G^{-k}P\): \(\rho(G)\ge 1\), unbounded \(P\), or \(0\in\partial P\). When these are removed (Schur stability, bounded \(P\), and \(0\in\operatorname{int}P\)), the paper gives a pseudo-polynomial bound on a finite \(r\) with \(S=S_r\) and develops SDP-based inner approximations aligned with the objective.

The forward-citing literature included here does not resolve the general decidability question for arbitrary rational \(G\) (notably in the marginally stable/unstable regimes that the source paper flags as delicate and related to Skolem/Pisot-type problems). Instead, it advances algorithmic understanding in restricted settings and via certification/approximation. Work on maximal invariant set computation under Schur stability and compact constraints provides finite-termination criteria (often LMI/S-procedure based) that, in the stable regime, effectively yield decision procedures for membership by computing \(O_\infty\) exactly. In parallel, the “safe learning” line of work develops exact conic reformulations for finite-horizon safety (\(T=1,2\)) and, for \(T=\infty\), emphasizes hardness and turns to SOS/SDP inner approximations under stability assumptions—conceptually mirroring the inner-approximation agenda of Ahmadi–Günlük but without addressing exact infinite-horizon membership.

Overall, the state of the art supports: (i) efficient exact membership/feasibility checks in important stable/compact regimes where \(S\) becomes polyhedral after finitely many steps or can be captured by invariant-set computations, and (ii) increasingly powerful convex-optimization-based certificates (ellipsoids, intersections of ellipsoids, piecewise semi-ellipsoids, support-function conditions) that can certify \(z\in S\) (sufficient conditions) or produce tight inner/outer approximations. The main gap remains the general decidability of exact membership for rational \(G,P,z\) in higher dimensions without stability/interiority/boundedness assumptions; this is precisely where connections to deep open problems on linear recurrence positivity/Skolem-type questions suggest that new ideas from logic/number theory and linear dynamical systems will be needed.

sources.title: Computation of the maximal invariant set of discrete-time linear systems subject to a class of non-convex constraints
sources.theorem_or_result: For discrete-time linear systems \,\(x(t+1)=Ax(t)\) with \(A\) Schur stable and compact constraint set \(X=\Omega\setminus\Theta\) where \(\Omega\) is given by quadratic inequalities and \(\Theta\) by “quasi-smooth” nonlinear inequalities admitting quadratic bounds, the paper gives LMI-based stopping criteria (via the S-procedure) that guarantee finite-time termination of an iterative algorithm and exact computation of the maximal constraint-admissible invariant set \(O_\infty=\bigcap_{k\ge 0}\{x: A^k x\in X\}\). In particular, for purely quadratic constraints (\(\Theta=\mathbb R^n\)), Theorem 1 states: there exists finite \(k^*\) such that an LMI quantity \(R_{\max}(k^*)\le 0\) and then \(O_\infty=O_{k^*}\) (the iterate of the standard preimage recursion). For semialgebraic constraints, Proposition 2 shows that after a polynomial lifting to a higher-dimensional linear system with quadratic constraints, the maximal invariant set of the original system equals the projection/pullback of the lifted maximal invariant set.
sources.connection: The open problem asks decidability of membership in \(S=\bigcap_{k\ge 0}\{x: G^k x\in P\}\) for rational \(G\), rational polyhedron \(P\), and rational query point \(z\). This paper studies computation of maximal invariant sets \(O_\infty=\bigcap_{k\ge 0}\{x: A^k x\in X\}\) and provides finite-time algorithms under strong assumptions (notably \(A\) Schur stable and constraints that are quadratic/quasi-smooth or semialgebraic after lifting). In the special case where \(X=P\) is a polyhedron and \(A=G\) is Schur stable, their framework reduces to the classical polyhedral invariant-set recursion which terminates in finite time, yielding a decision procedure for membership of \(z\) in \(S\) in that stable case. However, the open problem has no stability assumption and allows arbitrary rational \(G\); the paper does not address undecidable/hard cases (e.g., unstable or marginally stable dynamics) nor provide a general decidability result for all rational \(G\). Thus it gives partial progress/algorithms for an important restricted regime (stable dynamics, certain constraint classes), but not a full solution.

sources.theorem_or_result:
For linear dynamics with polyhedral safety set \(S=\{x: h_i^T x\le b_i\}\) and uncertainty sets over the unknown matrix \(A_\star\), the paper gives tractable conic representations of robust safety sets. In particular:
- (T=1) Proposition 1: the one-step robust safe set \(\{x\in S: Ax\in S\ \forall A\in U_k\}\) (with \(U_k\) a polyhedron of matrices consistent with data) is exactly the projection of an explicit linear program obtained by LP duality.
- (T=\infty) Theorem 18: for polyhedral \(S\) and polyhedral \(U_k\) consisting of Schur-stable matrices, it constructs SOS/SDP-representable inner approximations \(\tilde S^{\infty}_{k,d}\subseteq S^{\infty}_k:=\bigcap_{A\in U_k}\{x: A^t x\in S\ \forall t\ge0\}\), with \(\tilde S^{\infty}_{k,d}\) full-dimensional for large enough degree \(d\).
sources.connection:
The open problem asks decidability of membership for \(S=\bigcap_{k\ge0}\{x: AG^k x\le b\}\) for a fixed rational matrix \(G\) and rational polyhedron \(P\). This paper does not address decidability/complexity of exact membership for the infinite-horizon polyhedral invariance set for a given \(G\). Instead it:
- treats a related membership/feasibility question for robust safety sets under uncertainty over \(A\), and shows exact LP/SDP formulations for finite horizons \(T=1,2\);
- for \(T=\infty\), explicitly notes intractability: even for singleton \(U_0=\{A\}\), deciding feasibility of \(x\) in the infinite-horizon constraints is NP-hard (citing Ahmadi–Günlük 2024, Thm 2.1), and therefore provides only SOS/SDP inner approximations \(\tilde S^{\infty}_{k,d}\subseteq S^{\infty}_k\).
Thus it provides partial progress in the sense of (i) clarifying hardness of the exact membership problem (NP-hardness) and (ii) giving tractable sufficient conditions/inner approximations for infinite-horizon safety, but it does not resolve decidability of exact membership for rational \(G,P,z\).

sources.title: Safely learning dynamical systems from short trajectories
sources.theorem_or_result: For unknown linear dynamics with polytopic uncertainty set \(U_k\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) and polyhedral safety set \(S=\{x: h_i^T x\le b_i\}\), the robust one-step safe query problem \(\min_x c^T x\) s.t. \(x\in S\) and \(Ax\in S\ \forall A\in U_k\) admits an exact linear programming reformulation (Theorem 1). For ellipsoidal \(U_k\), the robust two-step safe query problem requiring \(\{x,Ax,A^2x\}\subseteq S\ \forall A\in U_k\) admits an exact semidefinite programming reformulation (Theorem 8).
sources.connection: The open problem asks for decidability of infinite-horizon polyhedral invariance membership: given rational \(G,P,z\), decide whether \(AG^k z\le b\) for all \(k\ge 0\). This paper does not address the infinite-horizon (\(T=\infty\)) membership/decidability question. Instead it gives exact conic (LP/SDP/SOCP) characterizations for finite-horizon safety sets \(S_k^T=\cap_{f\in U_k} S^T(f)\) with \(T\in\{1,2\}\) under uncertainty in the dynamics. It explicitly notes that handling \(T=\infty\) is left for future work, suggesting use of set-invariance tools (Ahmadi–Günlük 2018), but provides no algorithm/decidability result for the infinite intersection \(\cap_{k\ge 0} G^{-k}P\). Thus it is only indirectly related as finite-step robust safety is a truncation/approximation of the invariant-set condition.

sources.title: Piecewise semi-ellipsoidal control invariant sets
sources.theorem_or_result:
The paper develops a convex-programming (semidefinite programming) method to compute control-invariant sets for discrete-time linear (and switched) control systems under polyhedral state constraints, using the template of piecewise semi-ellipsoids. A central characterization is Theorem 2: for the control system 
\[x_{k+1}=Ax_k+Bu_k,\quad x_k\in X,\]
control invariance of a closed convex set \(S\subseteq X\) containing the origin is equivalent to the dual-space inclusion
\[S^* \supseteq A^\top P_{\mathrm{Im}(B)^\perp}^\top\, P_{\mathrm{Im}(B)^\perp}^{-\top} S^*,\]
which leads (via Theorem 3/Program 1) to an SDP feasibility program enforcing invariance and constraints for a piecewise semi-ellipsoidal gauge.
sources.connection: The open problem asks for decidability of membership in the maximal \(P\)-invariant set \(S=\bigcap_{k\ge 0}\{x:AG^k x\le b\}\) for an autonomous linear map \(G\) and polyhedral \(P\). This paper does not address decidability/complexity of the universal condition \(AG^k z\le b\ \forall k\ge 0\), nor does it give an algorithm that decides membership in \(S\) for rational \((A,b,G,z)\). Instead it studies *synthesis/approximation* of (control) invariant sets using convex optimization and duality (support/gauge, polars), primarily for controlled systems \(x^+=Ax+Bu\) (and switched variants). The autonomous case appears only as background (LMIs for ellipsoidal invariance, inequalities like \(g(S,x)\ge g(S,Ax)\)), which is conceptually related to invariance but does not resolve the membership-decidability question for polyhedral constraints.

sources.title: Geometric control of hybrid systems
sources.theorem_or_result:
The paper gives necessary and sufficient conditions for (controlled/weak) invariance of closed convex sets for linear hybrid systems in terms of support functions. In particular, for a linear hybrid algebraic system with mode constraints, weak invariance of convex sets \((S_q)\) is equivalent to the support-function inequalities:
- for each transition \(q\to_\sigma q'\): \(\delta^*(C_\sigma^\top y\mid S_q)\le \delta^*(E_\sigma^\top y\mid S_{q'})\) for all \(y\);
- for each mode \(q\): \(\langle z, C_q x\rangle\le 0\) for all \(z\) and all \(x\in F_{S_q}(E_q^\top z)\) (equivalently, when differentiable, \(\langle z, C_q\nabla\delta^*(E_q^\top z\mid S_q)\rangle\le 0\)).
They specialize these to tractable sufficient/necessary conditions for ellipsoids (LMIs), polynomial support functions (SOS constraints), and piecewise semi-ellipsoids.
sources.connection: The open problem asks decidability of membership in the maximal \(P\)-invariant set \(S=\bigcap_{k\ge0}\{x:AG^k x\le b\}\) for a single rational linear map \(G\) and rational polyhedron \(P\). This paper does not address decidability/complexity of the membership problem \(AG^k z\le b\ \forall k\) nor provide an algorithm that decides it for arbitrary rational \((A,b,G,z)\). Instead, it develops convex-analytic characterizations and computational relaxations for synthesizing controlled invariant sets for hybrid systems using support functions (often via LMIs/SOS). These techniques could be used to compute inner approximations of invariant sets for linear dynamics (including discrete-time linear maps as a special case), which may help certify that a given \(z\) is invariant (sufficient condition), but they do not yield a complete decision procedure for exact membership in \(S\) for polyhedral \(P\).

sources.title: On the convergence of the backward reachable sets of robust controlled invariant sets for discrete-time linear systems
sources.theorem_or_result:
For discrete-time linear systems with control and bounded additive disturbances 
\(x(t+1)=Ax(t)+Bu(t)+Ed(t)\) under convex compact constraints, the paper proves: if a compact convex robust controlled invariant set \(C_0\) satisfies \(C_0\subseteq \operatorname{int}(C_{k_0})\) for some finite \(k_0>0\) (equivalently \(C_0\subseteq \operatorname{int}(C_\infty)\) where \(C_k=\operatorname{Pre}^k(C_0)\)), then \(C_k\) converges to the maximal RCIS \(C_{\max}\) in Hausdorff distance with an exponential rate, i.e. there exist \(N_0\ge 0\), \(N>0\), \(c>0\), \(a\in(0,1)\) such that \(d(C_{N_0+kN},C_{\max})\le c a^k\) for all \(k\ge 0\). The condition \(C_0\subseteq \operatorname{int}(C_{k})\) can be checked for polytopes via an LP.
sources.connection: The open problem asks for decidability of membership in an infinite intersection \(S=\bigcap_{k\ge 0}\{x:AG^k x\le b\}\) for autonomous linear dynamics \(x_{k+1}=Gx_k\) and polyhedral \(P\). This paper does not address decidability/complexity of checking \(AG^k z\le b\) for all \(k\), nor does it provide an algorithm that decides membership in the maximal invariant set for arbitrary rational \(G,A,b,z\). Instead it studies convergence of iterative backward-reachability (Pre) computations for robust controlled invariant sets (with control and disturbances) and gives sufficient conditions ensuring convergence to the maximal RCIS and an exponential convergence rate. In the disturbance-free, no-control special case, its results relate to invariant-set approximation algorithms (inside-out) that could be used to approximate \(S\), but they do not yield a general decision procedure for exact membership.

For combinatorial auctions with multidimensional signals, is separability a necessary condition for achieving constant approximation to welfare? This problem is open even for single-dimensional signals and even for “simple” combinatorial valuations, such as unit demand.
title: Constant-factor welfare approximation without separability in multidimensional-signal combinatorial auctions
background_latex:
Consider a combinatorial auction with a set of agents  \( [n]=\{1,\dots,n\}\) and a set of items \( [m]=\{1,\dots,m\}\). An allocation is a partition of items into disjoint bundles \((T_1,\dots,T_n)\) with \(T_i\subseteq [m]\) and \(T_i\cap T_{i'}=\emptyset\) for \(i\neq i'\); agent \(i\) receives bundle \(T_i\) (possibly \(\emptyset\)).

Signals are multidimensional over bundles: for every agent \(j\in[n]\) and every bundle \(T\subseteq [m]\), agent \(j\) has a private signal \(s_{jT}\in\mathbb{R}_+\). For each bundle \(T\subseteq[m]\), let \(s_T=(s_{1T},\dots,s_{nT})\in\mathbb{R}_+^n\). The full signal profile is \(s=\{s_T\}_{T\subseteq[m]}\).

Valuations are interdependent: for each agent \(i\in[n]\) and bundle \(T\subseteq[m]\), the value of agent \(i\) for receiving bundle \(T\) is a known function \(v_{iT}(s_T)\in\mathbb{R}_+\) of the entire bundle-specific signal vector \(s_T\). Each \(v_{iT}\) is assumed (as in the paper’s model) to be weakly increasing in every coordinate of \(s_T\) and strictly increasing in the agent’s own signal coordinate \(s_{iT}\).

Incentives: a (possibly randomized) direct-revelation mechanism maps reported signals to an allocation and payments. The incentive notion of interest is universal ex post incentive compatibility with ex post individual rationality (universally ex post IC-IR): the mechanism is a distribution over deterministic mechanisms, each of which makes truthful reporting an ex post Nash equilibrium and guarantees nonnegative utility to truthful agents.

Objective: social welfare at signal profile \(s\) under allocation \((T_1,\dots,T_n)\) is \(\sum_{i=1}^n v_{iT_i}(s_{T_i})\). The optimal welfare is the maximum of this quantity over all feasible allocations.

Valuation structure: the paper focuses on the class of valuations that are submodular over signals (SOS). Informally, for each \(v_{iT}\), the marginal increase from raising a single coordinate \(s_{jT}\) is weakly larger when the other coordinates of \(s_T\) are smaller (a diminishing-returns property on \(\mathbb{R}_+^n\)). The paper obtains constant-factor welfare approximations in the multidimensional-signal model only under an additional structural assumption called separability, where \(v_{iT}(s_T)\) can be decomposed as a sum of a term depending only on other agents’ signals and a term depending only on \(i\)’s own signal.

The open question is whether such separability is actually required for constant-factor approximation in the multidimensional-signal combinatorial-auction model under SOS valuations.
problem_definition_latex: Determine whether there exists a universally ex post IC-IR mechanism \(\mathcal{M}\) and a universal constant \(c\ge 1\) such that, for every instance of a combinatorial auction with multidimensional bundle-specific signals \(s=\{s_T\}_{T\subseteq[m]}\) and SOS valuation functions \(\{v_{iT}:\mathbb{R}_+^n\to\mathbb{R}_+\}_{i\in[n],\,T\subseteq[m]}\) (with no separability assumption), the expected welfare achieved by \(\mathcal{M}\) at every signal profile \(s\) is at least \(\frac{1}{c}\) times the optimal welfare at \(s\).

counterexample_suitability_rationale: The question asks whether separability is necessary, so a counterexample would be a concrete SOS valuation family where every universally ex post IC-IR mechanism has super-constant (or unbounded) approximation ratio. Such hardness can often be explored by automated search over small instances (few agents/items, discrete signal grids) while encoding ex post IC constraints (e.g., via cycle-monotonicity) and optimizing the best achievable welfare ratio.

literature_review.synthesis:
Eden et al. (2023) introduce SOS (submodular-over-signals) as a substitutes-like condition on interdependent valuations and show that random partitioning of agents into “certain losers” and “potential winners” yields truthful welfare approximation because winners’ allocations are computed using proxy values that ignore other winners’ signals. The key technical step is their Lemma 2: for a d-SOS function \(v\), if one zeros out a uniformly random subset of other agents’ signals, the expected remaining value is at least \(\frac{1}{d+1}v(s)\). This underpins their constant-factor mechanisms in single-parameter environments and, under an additional separability condition \(v_{iT}(s_T)=g_{-i,T}(s_{-i,T})+h_{iT}(s_{iT})\), their RS-VCG mechanism achieving a 4-approximation for combinatorial auctions with multidimensional bundle-specific signals.

Subsequent work has made substantial progress on removing structural assumptions in restricted feasibility environments, but not yet in the full combinatorial-auction model with bundle-specific multidimensional signals. Several papers obtain constant (and sometimes tight) welfare approximations for SOS interdependent valuations in single-item or matroid single-parameter settings, improving constants (e.g., a tight factor 2 for binary signals) and developing new techniques such as candidate filtering and LP-duality “eating” processes. These advances demonstrate that separability is not inherently necessary for constant approximation in single-parameter settings, and they suggest alternative analytic frameworks (e.g., self-bounding/d-critical hierarchies) that might generalize.

However, none of the forward-citing papers provides a universally ex post IC-IR constant-factor welfare approximation for general heterogeneous combinatorial auctions with multidimensional bundle-specific signals \(\{s_{jT}\}\) under SOS valuations without separability, nor do they prove an impossibility specific to that auction model. Related negative evidence appears in the public-projects analogue, where universal truthfulness can force \(1/m\) approximations even under separable SOS unless exclusion is allowed, hinting that additional structure (beyond SOS) may be required in richer outcome spaces. At present, the separability barrier in Eden et al.’s RS-VCG payments remains the central obstacle: without separability, an agent’s report can affect the externality terms needed for VCG-style truthful payments, and new payment/estimation ideas seem necessary to obtain constant-factor welfare in the multidimensional-signal combinatorial setting.

sources.title: Constant approximation for private interdependent valuations
sources.theorem_or_result: They design the Randomized Candidate Filtering (RCF) mechanism for single-item auctions with private signals and private valuation functions. For any profile of valuation functions that are d-self-bounding over signals, RCF is EPIC-IR, polynomial-time, feasible with normalization \(\eta=2(d+1)\), and achieves welfare at least \(\frac{1}{\Theta(d)}\) of optimum (Theorem 4.1). In particular, for SOS valuations over signals: monotone SOS are 1-self-bounding and yield a \(8\ln 2\approx 5.55\)-approximation; general (possibly non-monotone) SOS are 2-self-bounding and yield a \(12\ln 2\approx 8.32\)-approximation. They also extend to \(m\) identical items with unit-demand bidders with \(O(d)\)-approximation (Theorem 5.1).
sources.connection: The open problem asks for a universally ex post IC-IR constant-factor welfare approximation in *combinatorial auctions* with multidimensional, bundle-specific signals \(s_{jT}\) and SOS valuations \(v_{iT}(s_T)\), *without* separability. This paper achieves constant-factor approximation without separability only in much more restricted allocation environments: single-item auctions (and multi-unit with identical items and unit-demand). It does not address general combinatorial allocations over heterogeneous items nor the bundle-specific multidimensional signal model; its mechanisms and analysis rely on comparing scalar values \(v_i(s)\) and lower estimates \(v_j(s_{-i})\) in a single-parameter allocation setting. Thus it provides partial progress/techniques (randomized discretization + random tie-breaking; self-bounding hierarchy) but does not resolve the combinatorial-auction open question.

sources.title: Interdependent public projects
sources.theorem_or_result:
Main welfare-approximation results for interdependent public projects with SOS valuations:
- (Impossibility) There exist separable SOS (indeed linear) valuation functions for which no universally ex post IC-IR mechanism can guarantee better than a 
\(1/m\)-approximation to optimal welfare (Theorem 4.5).
- (Possibility with exclusion) For excludable public projects with separable SOS valuations, a Random-Sampling-VCG mechanism is universally ex post IC-IR and achieves a \(1/4\)-approximation to optimal welfare (Theorem 4.7).
sources.connection:
The open problem asks whether separability is necessary for constant-factor welfare approximation in multidimensional-signal combinatorial auctions under SOS valuations (without separability), with universal ex post IC-IR.

This paper does not resolve that question for combinatorial auctions. It studies a different setting—interdependent public projects (a social choice/public goods analogue)—and shows that even with separability+SOS, universal truthfulness may be too restrictive: without excludability, no universally truthful mechanism beats random choice (\(1/m\)) (Theorem 4.5). It also highlights that the known constant-factor SOS mechanisms rely on an exclusion step, and adapts the Eden et al. [23] random-sampling/exclusion idea to excludable public projects to recover a constant factor (Theorem 4.7).

Thus, relative to the auction open problem, the paper provides evidence that additional structure beyond SOS (such as exclusion, and in their positive results also separability) may be essential, but it neither gives a constant-factor mechanism for non-separable SOS auctions nor proves impossibility for auctions without separability.

sources.title: Price of anarchy of simple auctions with interdependent values
sources.theorem_or_result: The paper studies Bayesian Price of Anarchy (B-PoA) of simple (non-truthful) auctions under interdependent values. For multi-item unit-demand settings with multidimensional per-item signals, it defines a parameter b3-heterogeneity and a limited-information-asymmetry condition b4\cdot \mathrm{Opt}^g\ge \mathrm{Opt} (where \(\mathrm{Opt}^g\) is welfare under truncated values). It proves (Theorem 4.7) that when \(n\ge m\), for \u0003b3-heterogeneous, \(c\)-single-crossing valuations, simultaneous privatized second-price auctions have B-PoA \(O(\delta\,\max\{\u03b3,c\}^2)\) under no-overbidding. It also proves strong lower bounds: even for \u03b3=c=1 common-value unit-demand instances with \(m=n^2\), every simultaneous item-bidding mechanism has \(\mathrm{Opt}/\mathrm{Eq}=\Omega(\tilde{\log} n)\) under no-overbidding (Theorem 5.1).
sources.connection: The open problem asks for a universally ex post IC-IR mechanism achieving a constant-factor welfare approximation for combinatorial auctions with bundle-specific multidimensional signals and SOS valuations, without separability. This paper does not design truthful (universally ex post IC-IR) mechanisms for that general combinatorial-auction model; instead it analyzes equilibrium inefficiency (PoA) of simple simultaneous item auctions, mainly for unit-demand bidders with per-item signals, under single-crossing/heterogeneity and (in the multi-item positive result) a submodularity-in-others condition plus a market information-asymmetry restriction. Thus it does not resolve whether separability is necessary for constant-factor truthful approximation under SOS. However, it is related in that it (i) works in multidimensional-signal IDV settings, (ii) uses submodularity-type assumptions over signals, and (iii) provides both positive and negative results showing additional structural/market assumptions are needed for good welfare guarantees in multi-item IDV settings.

sources.title: Auctions with interdependence and sos: improved approximation
sources.theorem_or_result: The paper proves that for single-item auctions with binary signals and interdependent valuations that are submodular over signals (SOS), there exists an ex post IC-IR randomized mechanism achieving a tight 2-approximation to welfare: for every signal profile \(s\in\{0,1\}^n\), \(\sum_i x_i(s)v_i(s)\ge \tfrac12\max_i v_i(s)\) (Theorem 1). The allocation rule uses only probabilities \(0\) and \(1/2\), and the approach extends to matroid single-parameter feasibility constraints (Appendix C).
sources.connection: The open problem asks for a universally ex post IC-IR constant-factor welfare approximation in *combinatorial auctions* with *multidimensional bundle-specific signals* \(s_{jT}\) and SOS valuations \(v_{iT}(s_T)\), *without* the separability assumption used by Eden et al. This paper does not address that model: it studies single-item (and matroid single-parameter) environments with one binary signal per bidder (not per bundle, not multidimensional over bundles), and welfare is \(\max_i v_i(s)\) rather than combinatorial allocation over items. Thus it does not resolve whether separability is necessary in the multidimensional-signal combinatorial-auction setting. It is nonetheless related as it develops tighter truthful approximation techniques under SOS and discusses (limited) progress beyond binary signals (Appendix D), which may inform attempts in richer models.

sources.title: Better approximation for interdependent SOS valuations
sources.theorem_or_result: The paper studies the single-item interdependent-values setting with one-dimensional signals and SOS valuations. It gives a polynomial-time ex post IC-IR mechanism achieving welfare approximation ratio \(3.31543\) (improving the prior \(4\)-approximation), by mixing (i) a contribution-based allocation rule and (ii) a biased random-sampling mechanism; see Theorem 4.
sources.connection: The open problem asks for a constant-factor welfare approximation in multidimensional-signal combinatorial auctions under SOS valuations without separability, with universal ex post IC-IR. This paper does not address multidimensional bundle-specific signals nor combinatorial allocations; it restricts to the canonical single-item auction with scalar signals \(s_i\) and valuations \(v_i(s)\). Thus it does not resolve whether separability is necessary in the multidimensional-signal combinatorial-auction model. At most, it provides improved techniques/lemmas for SOS (e.g., Lemma 2 bounding summed marginal losses) and improved approximation in a much simpler special case, which might inspire mechanisms for richer settings.

sources.title: Private interdependent valuations: New bounds for single-item auctions and matroids
sources.theorem_or_result:
The paper proves constant-factor truthful welfare approximations for private interdependent valuations in single-parameter environments: (i) for single-item auctions with private SOS valuations, an EPIC-IR “eating mechanism” achieves a 5-approximation to optimal welfare (Theorem 3.1); (ii) for matroid feasibility constraints with private d-critical valuations, an EPIC-IR mechanism achieves the tight 
\((d+1)\)-approximation (Theorem 4.1).
sources.connection: The open problem asks for a universally ex post IC-IR constant-factor welfare approximation for combinatorial auctions with multidimensional, bundle-specific signals and SOS valuations, without the separability assumption used in Eden et al. (2019). This citing paper does not address that multidimensional-signal combinatorial-auction model: it studies (a) single-item auctions (one item) with one signal per bidder (not bundle-specific multidimensional signals), and (b) matroid feasibility constraints over bidders (single-parameter service selection), not allocation of multiple items into bundles. While it improves SOS approximation for the single-item case (5-approx) and develops LP-duality/eating-process techniques that might be conceptually relevant, it neither removes separability in the multidimensional-signal combinatorial-auction setting nor provides a mechanism for that setting.

This is because the most general contraction type lemma for vector valued Lipschitz functions we know of only works for the \(\ell_2\)-norm [17]. title: Extend vector-contraction inequalities for Rademacher complexity to general norms
background_latex:
Let \(\mathcal X\) be an input (feature) space and \(\mathcal H\) be a class of vector-valued hypotheses \(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R^d\). Fix an i.i.d. sample \(x_1,\dots,x_n\in\mathcal X\). The (multivariate) empirical Rademacher complexity of \(\mathcal H\) is
\[
\widehat{\mathfrak R}_n(\mathcal H):=\mathbb E_{\sigma}\Big[\sup_{f\in\mathcal H}\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n \sigma_i^\top f(x_i)\Big],
\]
where \(\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_n\in\{\pm1\}^d\) have i.i.d. Rademacher coordinates and \(\mathbb E_\sigma\) denotes expectation over these signs.

Let \(\|\cdot\|\) be a norm on \(\mathbb R^d\). Consider a real-valued function \(\phi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) that is \(L\)-Lipschitz with respect to \(\|\cdot\|\), i.e.,
\[
|\phi(u)-\phi(v)|\le L\,\|u-v\|\quad\text{for all }u,v\in\mathbb R^d.
\]
Define the composed scalar class \(\phi\circ\mathcal H:=\{x\mapsto \phi(f(x)):\ f\in\mathcal H\}\). Its empirical Rademacher complexity is
\[
\widehat{\mathfrak R}_n(\phi\circ\mathcal H):=\mathbb E_{\epsilon}\Big[\sup_{f\in\mathcal H}\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n \epsilon_i\,\phi(f(x_i))\Big],
\]
where \(\epsilon_1,\dots,\epsilon_n\in\{\pm1\}\) are i.i.d. Rademacher signs.

A vector-contraction inequality is a bound that controls \(\widehat{\mathfrak R}_n(\phi\circ\mathcal H)\) in terms of \(L\) and \(\widehat{\mathfrak R}_n(\mathcal H)\) (or a closely related complexity), possibly with a constant depending on the choice of norm \(\|\cdot\|\). Known general results (e.g., Maurer 2016) provide such inequalities in the case \(\|\cdot\|=\|\cdot\|_2\), and some related results exist for \(\|\cdot\|_\infty\), but general norms (including general \(\ell_q\) norms) are not covered by the currently available contraction tools referenced by the paper.
problem_definition_latex:
Develop a vector-contraction inequality for empirical Rademacher complexity for Lipschitz maps under a general norm \(\|\cdot\|\) on \(\mathbb R^d\): find conditions and an explicit bound of the form
\[
\widehat{\mathfrak R}_n(\phi\circ\mathcal H)\le C(\|\cdot\|)\,L\,\widehat{\mathfrak R}_n(\mathcal H)
\]
(or an analogous bound in terms of a suitable multivariate Rademacher complexity), where \(\phi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz with respect to \(\|\cdot\|\), \(\mathcal H\subseteq\{f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R^d\}\), and \(C(\|\cdot\|)\) is an explicit constant or function of the norm, extending the known \(\ell_2\)-based vector-contraction inequality to general norms (including general \(\ell_q\) norms).
