title: Prove sharp decay rates for nonlinear comparison ODE driven by SDE noise
background_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex and continuously differentiable with \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient, and assume the minimizer set \(S=\operatorname{argmin} f\neq\emptyset\). Consider the stochastic differential equation (SDE)
\[
 dX(t)=-\nabla f(X(t))\,dt+\sigma(t,X(t))\,dW(t),\qquad t\ge 0,
\]
where \(W\) is an \(m\)-dimensional Brownian motion and \(\sigma:\mathbb{R}_+\times\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^{d\times m}\) is measurable, globally bounded in Frobenius norm, and Lipschitz in \(x\) uniformly in \(t\). Define the worst-case diffusion magnitude
\[
\sigma_\infty(t):=\sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}^d}\|\sigma(t,x)\|_F.
\]
Assume \(\sigma_\infty\in L^2(\mathbb{R}_+)\), so the noise vanishes in a square-integrable way.

Assume further that \(f\) satisfies a local error-bound / \L ojasiewicz-type condition near \(S\), leading (after localization arguments) to differential inequalities for certain nonnegative quantities \(y(t)\) (e.g., \(y(t)=\mathbb{E}[f(X(t)) - \min f]\) restricted to high-probability events, or \(y(t)=\mathbb{E}[\mathrm{dist}(X(t),S)^2/2]\) similarly restricted).

In the analysis, one is led to study a nonlinear scalar ODE (comparison equation)
\[
 y'(t)=-a\,y(t)^b+p_\delta(t),\qquad t>\hat t_\delta,
\]
with parameters \(a>0\), \(b>1\), an initial condition \(y(\hat t_\delta)=y_0(\hat t_\delta,\delta)>0\), and a nonnegative forcing term \(p_\delta(t)\) depending on the noise profile. The forcing term is of the same order as \(\sigma_\infty(t)^2\) (more precisely, \(p_\delta(t)=O(\sigma_\infty(t)^2)\) in the regime of interest), but it may also depend on \(\delta\) and \(\hat t_\delta\) through the localization step (Egorov-type arguments).
problem_definition_latex:
Assume \(a>0\), \(b>1\), and let \(p_\delta:[\hat t_\delta,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}_+\) be a measurable function satisfying \(p_\delta(t)=O(\sigma_\infty(t)^2)\). Assume also that
\[
\sigma_\infty(t)^2 = O\big((t+1)^{-\frac{b}{b-1}}\big)\qquad (t\to\infty),
\]
with constants independent of \(\delta\) and \(\hat t_\delta\). Consider the ODE
\[
 y'(t)=-a\,y(t)^b+p_\delta(t),\qquad t>\hat t_\delta,\qquad y(\hat t_\delta)=y_0(\hat t_\delta,\delta)>0.
\]
Establish that the corresponding solution satisfies the decay rate
\[
 y(t)=O\big((t+1)^{-\frac{1}{b-1}}\big)\qquad (t\to\infty).
\]
(Equivalently: prove the stated implication between the forcing decay \(p_\delta(t)\) at order \((t+1)^{-b/(b-1)}\) and the solution decay \(y(t)\) at order \((t+1)^{-1/(b-1)}\), uniformly with respect to the localization parameters \(\delta\) and \(\hat t_\delta\) as above.)

literature_review.synthesis:
In Maul\'en--Fadili--Attouch ("An SDE Perspective on Stochastic Convex Optimization"), the local \L ojasiewicz/error-bound analysis (Theorem 4.5) reduces, after Egorov-type localization on events \(\Omega_\delta\) and comparison (Lemma A.2), to bounding solutions of a nonlinear scalar comparison equation \(y'(t)=-a y(t)^b+p_\delta(t)\) with \(b>1\) and forcing \(p_\delta(t)\) of the same order as \(\sigma_\infty(t)^2\). The paper formulates Conjecture 4.11: if \(\sigma_\infty(t)^2=O((t+1)^{-b/(b-1)})\) (uniformly in the localization parameters) and \(p_\delta=O(\sigma_\infty^2)\), then the comparison solution should satisfy the sharp decay \(y(t)=O((t+1)^{-1/(b-1)})\). The difficulty is that the localization time \(\hat t_\delta\) depends on \(\delta\), and the forcing term inherits a nontrivial dependence on \(\delta\) through tail integrals such as \(\sigma_\infty(t)^2 / \sqrt[2q]{\int_{\hat t_\delta}^t \sigma_\infty(u)^2 du}\), so standard explicit ODE solutions do not directly yield uniform-in-\(\delta\) bounds.

Among forward citations, several works develop closely related dissipative-plus-noise differential inequalities and rate balances under error bounds or \L ojasiewicz/KL conditions, but none isolates and proves the conjectured sharp comparison principle in the generality needed here. "Stochastic inertial dynamics via time scaling and averaging" and the two Tikhonov-regularization papers for stochastic (sub)gradient flows in Hilbert spaces obtain explicit polynomial rates by balancing nonlinear dissipation against noise decay \(\sigma_\infty^2(t)=O(t^{-\alpha})\), providing techniques for tracking how diffusion tails enter remainders. "Continuous-time Analysis of a Stochastic ADMM Method for Nonconvex Composite Optimization" uses a comparison-lemma mechanism in a KL setting to derive exponential/polynomial rates with residual terms controlled by diffusion-energy tails \(U_t\), illustrating how additional assumptions on the forcing (e.g. \(\mathbb E[U_t]\le C/(t+1)^a\)) lead to explicit decay. Related-tool papers on stochastic heavy-ball dynamics and multiscale stochastic inclusions provide Lyapunov/martingale methods and tail-integral controls for vanishing diffusion, but focus mainly on ergodic or accelerated regimes rather than the sharp non-ergodic polynomial decay in Conjecture 4.11.

Overall, the open problem remains unsolved in the forward-citation set: a sharp, uniform (in \(\delta,\hat t_\delta\)) comparison-ODE lemma that converts forcing \(p_\delta(t)=O((t+1)^{-b/(b-1)})\) into solution decay \(y(t)=O((t+1)^{-1/(b-1)})\) would close the gap in the local \L ojasiewicz-rate theory for vanishing-noise SDE optimization. Promising directions suggested by the citing literature include: (i) refining nonlinear Gronwall/Bihari-type inequalities with explicit polynomial weights to handle forcing terms involving tail integrals; (ii) constructing explicit supersolutions of the form \(C(t+1)^{-1/(b-1)}\) with carefully chosen \(C\) that absorb the \(\delta\)-dependent prefactors; and (iii) leveraging regular variation/Karamata-type arguments to control expressions like \(\sigma_\infty(t)^2 / (\int_{\hat t_\delta}^t \sigma_\infty^2)^{1/(2q)}\) uniformly over \(\hat t_\delta\).

sources.theorem_or_result:
The paper proves convergence and rate results for stochastic inertial dynamics (S−ISIHD)/(S−ISIHDNS) by time-scaling/averaging reduction to a first-order stochastic (sub)gradient flow. In particular, under 
- convex smooth

the trajectory satisfies \(\mathbb E[f(X(t)) - \min f]=O(t^{-2})\) and \(f(X(t)) - \min f=o(t^{-2})\) a.s. (Corollary 3.5). They also give a local Polyak-

sources.connection:
The open problem asks for a sharp comparison-ODE decay: if \(y'(t)=-a y(t)^b + p(t)\) with \(b>1\) and forcing \(p(t)=O((t+1)^{-b/(b-1)})\), then \(y(t)=O((t+1)^{-1/(b-1)})\), uniformly over localization parameters. This paper does not analyze that scalar ODE directly. However, its local Polyak-

\L ojasiewicz analysis (Theorem 3.7) effectively controls a localized Lyapunov quantity by a differential inequality of the same general form (dissipative term plus noise term), and it derives explicit rates/remainders in terms of \(\sigma_\infty\) (through functions like \(l_\delta\) built from \(\sigma_\infty^2\) and its tail integral). Thus it provides partial progress/techniques toward handling the forcing-vs-decay interplay, but it does not establish the specific sharp polynomial implication \(p(t)=O(t^{-b/(b-1)})\Rightarrow y(t)=O(t^{-1/(b-1)})\) for the comparison ODE, nor the requested uniformity in \(\delta,\hat t_\delta\).

sources.title: Tikhonov regularization for stochastic non-smooth convex optimization in Hilbert spaces
sources.theorem_or_result:
In the smooth case with Tikhonov regularization, the paper proves explicit expectation rates for the stochastic flow
\[dX(t)=-\nabla f(X(t))dt- t^{-r}X(t)dt+\sigma(t,X(t))dW(t),\]
under a local Hölderian error bound \(f\in EB_p(S)\) and square-integrable, nonincreasing noise \(\sigma_\infty\in L^2\). In particular (Theorem 4.15), if \(\sigma_\infty^2(t)=O(t^{-\alpha})\) with \(\alpha>1\), then
- \(\mathbb E[f(X(t)) - \min f]=O(t^{-r}+R(t))\) with \(R(t)=O(t^{r-\alpha})\), hence \(\mathbb E[f(X(t)) - \min f]=O(t^{-\min\{r,\alpha-r\}})\).

sources.title: Stochastic differential inclusions and Tikhonov regularization for stochastic non-smooth convex optimization in Hilbert spaces
sources.theorem_or_result:
The paper proves convergence and explicit rates for stochastic subgradient/gradient flows (and Tikhonov-regularized variants) under vanishing diffusion 

- For (SDI) with 
\(dX(t)\in-\partial(f+g)(X(t))dt+\sigma(t,X(t))dW(t)\) and \(\sigma_\infty\in L^2\), Theorem 3.6 gives a.s. weak convergence to \(\operatorname{argmin}(f+g)\) and \(\int_{t_0}^\infty (F(X(t)) - \min F)dt<\infty\) (under continuity of \(g\)).

- For the smooth Tikhonov-regularized SDE 
\(dX(t)=-\nabla f(X(t))dt-t^{-r}X(t)dt+\sigma(t,X(t))dW(t)\), with \(f\in EB_p(S)\) and \(\sigma_\infty^2(t)=O(t^{-\alpha})\), Theorem 4.15 yields \(\mathbb E[f(X(t)) - \min f]=O(t^{-r}+R(t))\) with \(R(t)=O(t^{r-\alpha})\) (hence \(\mathbb E[f(X(t)) - \min f]=O(t^{-\min\{r,\alpha-r\}})\) when \(\alpha>1\)), and \(\mathbb E\|X(t)-x^\star\|^2=O(t^{-(1-r)}+t^{-r/p}+t^{-(\alpha-2r)})\) under stated parameter ranges.

The open problem asks for a sharp comparison-ODE estimate: if \(y'(t)=-a y(t)^b+p(t)\) with \(b>1\) and forcing \(p(t)=O((t+1)^{-b/(b-1)})\), then \(y(t)=O((t+1)^{-1/(b-1)})\), uniformly over localization parameters.

This paper does not directly analyze that scalar ODE or prove the stated implication in that generality. However, it addresses the same SDE/optimization setting (vanishing diffusion \(\sigma_\infty\in L^2\), local error bounds/Łojasiewicz via \(EB_p\)) and derives explicit polynomial decay rates for objective gaps and distances in expectation (Theorem 4.15) under assumptions of the form \(\sigma_\infty^2(t)=O(t^{-\alpha})\). sources.title: Continuous-time Analysis of a Stochastic ADMM Method for Nonconvex Composite Optimization
sources.theorem_or_result:
The paper proves convergence and convergence-rate bounds for the SDE model of stochastic proximal linearized ADMM:
- For the SDE 
\[dx(t)=-(1/\lambda)\nabla H_\mu(x(t))\,dt+(1/(\lambda\sqrt{\rho}))\,\sigma(x(t))\,dW(t),\]
with bounded Lipschitz diffusion \(\|\sigma(x)\|_F\le \bar\sigma\) and \(U_t:=\int_t^\infty \|\sigma(x(s))\|_F^2 ds\), if \(\mathbb E[U_0]<\infty\) then \(H_\mu(x(t))\) converges a.s. and \(\|\nabla H_\mu(x(t))\|\to 0\) a.s. (Theorem 2).
- Under a (uniformized) Lojasiewicz inequality with exponent \(\theta\in(0,1)\) and boundedness of \(x(t)\), they obtain in-expectation rates for the objective gap:
  - if \(\theta\in(0,1/2]\): \(\mathbb E|H_\mu(x(t))-H_{\mu,\infty}|\le a_1 e^{-b_1(t-T)}+c_1/\rho\);
  - if \(\theta\in(1/2,1)\): \(\mathbb E|H_\mu(x(t))-H_{\mu,\infty}|\le a_2 (t-T)^{1/(1-2\theta)}+c_2/\rho\) (Theorem 3).
- If additionally \(\mathbb E[U_t]\le C/(t+1)^a\) with \(a>1\), then \(x(t)\) converges a.s. to a critical point of \(H_\mu\) and they derive rates for \(\mathbb E\|x(t)-x_\infty\|\) (Theorems 4–5).
sources.connection:
The open problem asks for sharp polynomial decay of solutions to a scalar comparison ODE \(y'(t)=-a y(t)^b+p(t)\) when \(p(t)=O((t+1)^{-b/(b-1)})\), namely \(y(t)=O((t+1)^{-1/(b-1)})\), uniformly over localization parameters.

This paper does not analyze that scalar ODE directly, nor does it prove the stated sharp implication for general measurable \(p_\delta\). However, it uses essentially the same comparison-ODE mechanism (their Lemma 5) to control a Lyapunov gap \(L(t)=\mathbb E[L(x(t))]-\bar L\) via an inequality of the form
\[L(t)\le L(T)-b\int_T^t L(s)^{2\theta}\,ds + c(t-T),\]
which corresponds to the ODE template with exponent \(b=2\theta\) and forcing \(\approx c\) (or with additional forcing coming from \(\int E[U_s]^{2\theta} ds\)). They obtain explicit decay bounds (exponential when \(2\theta\le 1\), polynomial when \(2\theta>1\)) under stronger assumptions such as \(\mathbb E[U_t]\le C/(t+1)^a\) with \(a>1\).

Thus the paper provides related comparison-lemma technology and rate derivations in an SDE/KL setting, but it does not establish the specific sharp polynomial rate \((t+1)^{-1/(b-1)}\) from forcing \((t+1)^{-b/(b-1)}\) for the nonlinear ODE in the open problem, nor the uniformity in \(\delta,\hat t_\delta\).

sources.title: Long-Time Analysis of Stochastic Heavy Ball Dynamics for Convex Optimization and Monotone Equations
sources.theorem_or_result:
For stochastic Heavy Ball dynamics with friction (SHBF) in a Hilbert space,
- dY(t)=X(t)dt,
- dX(t)=(-\lambda X(t)-b(t)\nabla f(Y(t)))dt+\sigma_Y(t)dW(t),
assuming \(\int_{t_0}^\infty \|\sigma_Y(t)\|_{HS}^2dt<\infty\) and \(\sup_{t\ge t_0} \dot b(t)/b(t)<\lambda\), the authors prove almost sure rates \(f(Y(t)) - \inf f = o(1/b(t))\) and \(\|X(t)\|=o(1)\), and expected rate \(\mathbb E[f(Y(t)) - \inf f]=O(1/b(t))\) (Theorem 2.2). Under an additional integrability condition \(\int_{t_0}^\infty \frac{1}{b(s)}(\int_{(s+t_0)/2}^s b(r)dr)\|\sigma_Y(s)\|_{HS}^2ds<\infty\), they obtain improved a.s. bounds
\[f(Y(t)) - \inf f = O\Big(\frac{1}{\int_{(t+t_0)/2}^t b(s)ds}\Big),\qquad \|X(t)\| = O\Big(\sqrt{\frac{b(t)}{\int_{(t+t_0)/2}^t b(s)ds}}\Big).\]
They also transfer these results via time-rescaling to stochastic Su–Boyd–Cand\`es (SAVD), yielding \(f(Z(s)) - \inf f = o(1/s^2)\) a.s. and \(\mathbb E[f(Z(s)) - \inf f]=O(1/s^2)\) under \(\int s^2\|\sigma_Z(s)\|_{HS}^2ds<\infty\) (Theorem 2.7).
sources.connection: The open problem asks for sharp polynomial decay for solutions of a scalar comparison ODE \(y'(t)=-a y(t)^b+p_\delta(t)\) when \(p_\delta(t)\) decays like \((t+1)^{-b/(b-1)}\), uniformly in localization parameters. This paper does not study that scalar nonlinear ODE nor prove a general comparison lemma of the requested type. Instead it derives convergence rates for stochastic second-order optimization/monotone-operator dynamics using Lyapunov/energy estimates and martingale convergence (Mao’s theorem), under square-integrability (and sometimes stronger weighted integrability) assumptions on the diffusion. These techniques are related in spirit to controlling forcing/noise terms in differential inequalities, but they do not establish the specific implication \(p(t)=O((t+1)^{-b/(b-1)})\Rightarrow y(t)=O((t+1)^{-1/(b-1)})\) for the nonlinear comparison ODE, nor address uniformity in \(\delta,\hat t_\delta\).

sources.title: Asymptotic behaviour of coupled random dynamical systems with multiscale aspects
sources.theorem_or_result:
The paper studies stochastic differential inclusions of the form 
\[dX(t)+A(X(t))\,dt+\beta(t)\nabla\Psi(X(t))\,dt\ni\sigma(t,X(t))\,dW(t),\]
with maximally monotone drift part and vanishing diffusion magnitude \(\Sigma(t)=\sup_x\|\sigma(t,x)\|_F\in L^2(0,\infty)\). Under the Attouch–Czarnecki integrability condition \(\int_0^\infty \beta(t)\big(\Psi^*(p/\beta(t)) - s_C(p/\beta(t))\big)dt<\infty\) and standard Lipschitz assumptions on \(\sigma\), they prove almost sure asymptotic feasibility \(\Psi(X(t))\to 0\) and convergence of objective values in the potential case \(A=\partial\Phi\): \(\Phi(X(t))\to \min_C\Phi\) a.s. They also establish finite-time ergodic rates, e.g. for the Cesàro average \(\bar X(t)=t^{-1}\int_0^t X(s)ds\), 
\[\mathbb E[\Theta_\delta(\bar X(t))]=O(1/t),\qquad \mathbb E[\Phi(\bar X(t)) - \min_C\Phi]\le \frac{\mathrm{dist}(x,S)^2}{2t}+\frac{1}{2t}\int_0^t \Sigma(s)^2 ds.\]
sources.connection: The open problem asks for sharp polynomial decay of solutions to a scalar comparison ODE \(y'=-a y^b + p_\delta(t)\) when the forcing satisfies \(p_\delta(t)=O((t+1)^{-b/(b-1)})\), uniformly in localization parameters. This paper does not analyze that nonlinear comparison ODE nor prove the specific implication \(p(t)=O(t^{-b/(b-1)})\Rightarrow y(t)=O(t^{-1/(b-1)})\). Instead, it develops convergence and rate bounds for stochastic differential inclusions with vanishing noise \(\Sigma\in L^2\), yielding mainly ergodic \(O(1/t)\) rates for gap functions / objective gaps and almost sure convergence of values. These results could serve as background/tools for SDE-based optimization analyses, but they do not address the sharp non-ergodic polynomial decay regime governed by a \L ojasiewicz exponent \(b>1\) and a forcing term of order \(\Sigma(t)^2\).

title: Improve minimax regret dependence on states and horizon in episodic CTMDPs
background_latex:
Consider an episodic, finite-horizon continuous-time Markov decision process (CTMDP) with finite state space \(\mathcal S\) (\(|\mathcal S|=S\)), finite action space \(\mathcal A\) (\(|\mathcal A|=A\)), and fixed horizon \([0,H]\). When action \(a\in\mathcal A\) is chosen in state \(x\in\mathcal S\), the process stays in \(x\) for an exponentially distributed holding time with rate \(\lambda(x,a)\in[\lambda_{\min},\lambda_{\max}]\), accrues reward at rate \(r(x,a)\in[0,1]\) during the holding time, and then jumps to a next state \(Y\in\mathcal S\) with probability \(p(\cdot\mid x,a)\) (time-homogeneous). The parameters \(p\) and \(\lambda\) are unknown to the learning agent.

A (deterministic Markov) policy \(\pi\) maps a state and remaining time to an action: \(\pi:\mathcal S\times[0,H]\to\mathcal A\). Starting from a fixed initial state \(x_0\), define the (finite-horizon) value function
\[
V^{\pi}(x,t):=\mathbb E_{\pi}\Big[\int_0^{t} r(X(u),A(u))\,du\,\Big|\,X(0)=x\Big],\qquad (x,t)\in\mathcal S\times[0,H],
\]
and the optimal value \(V^*(x,t):=\sup_{\pi} V^{\pi}(x,t)\).

The agent interacts with the same unknown CTMDP over \(K\) independent episodes, each of length \(H\), restarting from \(x_0\) each episode. Let \(\pi_k\) be the policy used in episode \(k\). The (expected) cumulative regret after \(K\) episodes is
\[
\mathrm{Regret}(K):=\mathbb E\Big[\sum_{k=1}^K \big(V^*(x_0,H)-V^{\pi_k}(x_0,H)\big)\Big].
\]
A minimax (worst-case) regret rate studies \(\sup_{M\in\mathcal C}\mathrm{Regret}(K)\), where \(\mathcal C\) is the class of all such CTMDPs with given \((S,A,H,\lambda_{\min},\lambda_{\max})\) and bounded rewards.

In the referenced work, an upper bound of order \(\widetilde O(\sqrt K)\) is proved but with a leading dependence that is worse than the known lower bound in its dependence on \(S\), on \(H\), and on \(\lambda_{\max}\). In particular, their regret upper bound contains an extra factor \(\sqrt S\) (relative to discrete-time tight bounds) and a worse dependence on \(H\), while their lower bound scales on the order of \(H\sqrt{SAK}\) (up to constants and log factors) in a certain parameter regime.
problem_definition_latex:
Determine whether one can design an episodic reinforcement-learning algorithm for the above finite-horizon tabular CTMDP class \(\mathcal C\) whose worst-case expected regret \(\sup_{M\in\mathcal C}\mathrm{Regret}(K)\) improves the known upper bounds by reducing their dependence on \(S\), \(H\), and \(\lambda_{\max}\), thereby narrowing the gap to the known lower bounds (which already show \(\Omega(H\sqrt{SAK})\) scaling in \(K\) and \(A\) up to log factors).

Equivalently: improve the minimax, instance-independent regret upper bound for episodic finite-horizon tabular CTMDPs beyond the existing \(\widetilde O(\sqrt K)\) bound by achieving sharper polynomial dependence on \(S\), \(H\), and \(\lambda_{\max}\) (and ideally matching the lower bound up to logarithmic factors).

literature_review.synthesis:
The source paper (Gao & Zhou, 2023) establishes the first minimax-style \(\widetilde O(\sqrt K)\) regret guarantee for episodic finite-horizon tabular CTMDPs with unknown transition probabilities and holding-time rates, via CT-UCBVI: optimism over confidence sets combined with a continuous-time value-iteration operator \(G\) (built from \(T^a\) in (6)) and a contraction-based control of planning error. Their analysis highlights continuous-time-specific obstacles absent in discrete time: truncated holding times at the horizon, random and unbounded numbers of jumps per episode (handled via uniformization), and the need to estimate \(\lambda(x,a)\) from time-spent statistics rather than counts.

However, the resulting leading dependence on \(S\), \(H\), and \(\lambda_{\max}\) is not tight: the upper bound carries an extra \(\sqrt S\) factor (stemming from \(\ell_1\) concentration for the \(S\)-dimensional transition vector) and worse polynomial dependence on \(H\) and \(\lambda_{\max}\) than the lower bound. The paper’s lower bound construction (tree MDP with Erlang-distributed time-to-depth \(d\)) yields \(\Omega(H\sqrt{SAK})\) in a regime, matching the \(\sqrt K\) and \(\sqrt{SA}\) scaling but leaving a substantial gap in \(S\) and \(H\).

The only forward-citing work provided here does not close this gap. Gao & Zhou’s later work on average-reward CTMDPs develops refined continuous-time UCRL-style tools (confidence bounds for exponential holding times, uniformization, and point-process comparisons) but targets instance-dependent \(O(\log T)\) regret rather than episodic minimax rates. A separate intensity-control actor–critic paper develops martingale-based continuous-time policy-gradient machinery without regret bounds. Thus, based on the available forward citations, improving minimax episodic CTMDP regret dependence on \(S,H,\lambda_{\max}\) remains open; promising directions suggested by the source include importing variance-sensitive (Bernstein) bonuses or value-function-based confidence sets (as in UCBVI-BF/EULER) while coping with random jump counts and horizon truncation.

sources.title: Logarithmic regret bounds for continuous-time average-reward Markov decision processes
sources.theorem_or_result: The paper studies tabular continuous-time MDPs in the infinite-horizon average-reward setting with unknown transition probabilities \(p(\cdot\mid s,a)\) and holding-time rates \(\lambda(s,a)\in[\lambda_{\min},\lambda_{\max}]\). It proves an instance-dependent logarithmic regret lower bound: for any uniformly fast algorithm \(\mathcal G\) and any CTMDP \(M\), \[\liminf_{T\to\infty}\frac{\mathbb E[R_T^{\mathcal G}(s_0,M)]}{\log T}\ge C(M),\] where \(C(M)=\sum_{(s,a)\in B(M)} \phi^*(s,a;M)/K(s,a;M)\) is defined via suboptimality gaps \(\phi^*\) and KL-type information terms \(K\). It also proposes CT-UCRL and proves a finite-time gap-dependent upper bound (in decision epochs \(N\)): \[R_N^{\mathrm{CT\text{-}UCRL}}(s_0,M)\le \frac{4C\,\log N}{g}+C',\] where \(g\) is the average-reward policy gap and \(C\) scales polynomially in \(S,A,\lambda_{\max},\lambda_{\min}^{-1}\) and the diameter \(D(M)\) (e.g. \(C=\Theta(\lambda_{\max}^2 D(M)^2 S^2A + (\lambda_{\max}^2/\lambda_{\min}^2)SA)\) up to constants).
sources.connection: The open problem concerns minimax (instance-independent) regret for finite-horizon episodic CTMDPs and improving its dependence on \(S\), \(H\), and \(\lambda_{\max}\) toward \(\widetilde\Omega(H\sqrt{SAK})\). This paper does not address the episodic finite-horizon setting or minimax \(\widetilde O(\sqrt K)\) bounds; instead it studies infinite-horizon average-reward CTMDPs and derives instance-dependent \(O(\log T)\) regret (gap-dependent) plus matching logarithmic lower bounds for uniformly fast algorithms. Nevertheless, it contributes techniques potentially relevant to episodic CTMDPs: (i) careful estimation/confidence bounds for exponential holding times (truncated mean with sub-Gaussian tails), (ii) continuous-time UCRL-style optimism with an extended CTMDP and uniformization, and (iii) stochastic comparison of counting processes to relate decision-epoch and continuous-time regret. These tools might be adaptable when trying to sharpen \(S,H,\lambda_{\max}\) dependence in episodic minimax analyses, but the paper itself does not narrow the stated minimax gap.

sources.title: Reinforcement learning for intensity control: An application to choice-based network revenue management
sources.theorem_or_result:
The paper develops a continuous-time, event-driven actor–critic reinforcement-learning framework for intensity control problems (e.g., choice-based network revenue management) by adapting Monte Carlo / TD policy evaluation and policy-gradient methods to continuous time without upfront time discretization. Key theoretical statements include: (i) a martingale characterization of the policy value function (Proposition 1) and an equivalent martingale orthogonality condition (Theorem 2) for policy evaluation; (ii) an implementable continuous-time policy-gradient formula for jump/intensity-control dynamics (Theorem 3): \[

abla_\phi J(0,c;\pi_\phi)=\mathbb E\Big[\int_{(0,T]}\sum_{j=1}^n 
abla_\phi\log\pi_\phi(S_t\mid t,X_{t-}) ig(J(t,X_{t-}-A_j;\pi_\phi)-J(t,X_{t-};\pi_\phi)+p_j ig)\,dN_{j,t}^{\pi_\phi}+\gamma\int_0^T 
abla_\phi H(\pi_\phi(\cdot\mid t,X_{t-}))\,dt\Big].
\]

This paper does not study regret, minimax rates, or tabular exploration; it focuses on model-free actor–critic methods for a specific class of event-driven intensity control problems (Poisson arrivals, revenue-management structure), provides martingale-based foundations for policy evaluation/gradient, and reports empirical performance. While its event-driven ‘inherent discretization’ idea and martingale tools may be conceptually relevant to CTMDP algorithm design, it does not provide regret guarantees nor address the stated gap in \(S,H,\lambda_{\max}\) dependence.

title: Extend dimension-reduction integral-equation method to Wonham-filter drift uncertainty setting
background_latex:
Consider a continuous-time financial market on a filtered probability space supporting a risky asset price process \(S\) with volatility \(\sigma>0\), and an unobservable drift process \(\mu_t\) taking two values \(\mu_h>\mu_l\). The agent observes only the price filtration \(\mathcal F^S_t\) generated by \(S\), not \(\mu_t\) nor the driving Brownian motion.

In the paper’s baseline model, \(\mu\) is an \(\mathcal F_0\)-measurable two-point random variable and the conditional probability \(P_t=\mathbb P(\mu=\mu_h\mid\mathcal F^S_t)\) satisfies a Bayesian-filter SDE of the form \(dP_t=\Theta P_t(1-P_t)d\widetilde B_t\), where \(\Theta=(\mu_h-\mu_l)/\sigma\) and \(\widetilde B\) is the innovation Brownian motion. The authors then introduce the likelihood ratio \(\Phi_t:=\frac{P_t}{1-P_t}\) and a measure change \(\mathbb Q\) under which \(\Phi\) becomes a geometric Brownian motion, enabling a dimension reduction that converts an intractable free-boundary integral equation involving \(\mathbb E[\cdot]\) under the joint law of \((Y_t,P_t)\) into a solvable integral equation without unknown joint transition densities.

In the alternative setting highlighted in the conclusion, the unobservable drift is instead a hidden two-state continuous-time Markov chain \(\alpha_t\in\{h,l\}\) with generator
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
-\lambda_h & \lambda_h\\
\lambda_l & -\lambda_l
\end{pmatrix},\qquad \lambda_h,\lambda_l>0,
\]
and \(\mu_t=\mu(\alpha_t)\in\{\mu_h,\mu_l\}\). The conditional probability \(P_t:=\mathbb P(\alpha_t=h\mid\mathcal F^S_t)\) then follows the Wonham filter
\[

\]
with innovation process \(d\widetilde B_t = \sigma^{-1}dS_t/S_t - \mathbb E[\mu(\alpha_t)\mid\mathcal F^S_t]dt\).

\[

\]
for a \(\mathbb Q\)-Brownian motion \(W\). literature_review.synthesis:
In Xing–Ma–Zheng (2024), the key computational bottleneck is the Volterra free-boundary equation (their (3.9)) involving expectations under the joint law of the dual state \((Y_t,P_t)\). In the static two-point prior (Bayesian filter) case, they follow Klein’s likelihood-ratio idea: with \(\Phi_t=P_t/(1-P_t)\) and a Girsanov change of measure \(\mathbb Q\), \(\Phi\) becomes geometric Brownian motion and, crucially, \(F_t=(1+\Phi_t)/(1+\varphi)=\frac{d\mathbb P}{d\mathbb Q}\vert_{\mathcal F_t^S}\). This identity allows them to rewrite the dual stopping problem so that one state variable becomes a parameter, leading to a numerically tractable one-dimensional integral equation (their (3.19)).

The only forward-citing work provided, “S-shaped Utility Maximization with VaR Constraint and Partial Information,” develops closely related integral representations under partial information but remains in the same Bayesian-filter (static drift) setting and again relies on the same martingale likelihood-ratio identity \(F_t=(1+\Phi_t)/(1+\phi)\). It therefore does not address the Wonham-filter case highlighted as open in Xing–Ma–Zheng’s conclusion, where \(P_t\) has mean-reverting drift and \(\Phi_t\) satisfies \(d\Phi_t=(\lambda_l-\lambda_h\Phi_t)(1+\Phi_t)dt+\Theta\Phi_t dW_t\) under \(\mathbb Q\), breaking the simple Radon–Nikodym relationship and blocking the dimension reduction.

Based on the supplied citation set, there is currently no paper that resolves the requested extension to hidden Markov-chain drift uncertainty. The problem remains open: one needs either a different measure-change/augmentation that restores a tractable density process, or an alternative characterization (e.g., coupled integral equations for regime-conditioned components, or a PDE/IE system exploiting the finite-state structure) that avoids unknown joint transition densities while retaining numerical efficiency comparable to the Bayesian-filter reduction.

title: Equality between semi-strict and strict subgradient derivatives for C2-decomposable functions
background_latex:
Let \(Y\) be a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, and let \(g:Y\to\overline{\mathbb R}:=[-\infty,\infty]\) be a proper lower-semicontinuous convex function.

For \(\bar u\in Y\) with \(g(\bar u)<\infty\) and \(\bar y\in \partial g(\bar u)\), define:

1) The (limiting/convex) subdifferential \(\partial g(\bar u)\).

2) The subderivative (first-order epi-derivative)
\[
 dg(\bar u)(w):=\liminf_{t\downarrow 0,\,w'\to w}\frac{g(\bar u+t w')-g(\bar u)}{t}.
\]

3) The critical cone of \(g\) at \(\bar u\) for \(\bar y\):
\[
 K_g(\bar u,\bar y):=\{w\in Y\mid \langle \bar y,w\rangle = dg(\bar u)(w)\}.
\]

4) The second subderivative of \(g\) at \(\bar u\) for \(\bar y\), defined via second-order difference quotients
\[
\Delta_t^2 g(\bar u,\bar y)(w):=\frac{g(\bar u+t w)-g(\bar u)-t\langle \bar y,w\rangle}{\tfrac12 t^2},\qquad t>0,
\]
\[
 d^2 g(\bar u,\bar y)(w):=\liminf_{t\downarrow 0,\,w'\to w}\Delta_t^2 g(\bar u,\bar y)(w').
\]

5) The graphical derivative \(D(\partial g)(\bar u,\bar y)\) of the set-valued mapping \(\partial g\) at \((\bar u,\bar y)\), and the tangent cone \(T_{\partial g(\bar u)}(\bar y)\) to the (convex) set \(\partial g(\bar u)\) at \(\bar y\).

6) The semi-strict graphical derivative \(D^b(\partial g)(\bar u,\bar y)\) (as defined by the outer limit representation)
\[
 D^b(\partial g)(\bar u,\bar y)(w):=\limsup_{t\downarrow 0,\,w'\to w\,;\,y\to \bar y,\,y\in \partial g(\bar u)}\frac{\partial g(\bar u+t w')-y}{t}.
\]

The paper studies conditions under which one has the identity
\[
 D^b(\partial g)(\bar u,\bar y)(w)=\operatorname{cl}\Big(D(\partial g)(\bar u,\bar y)(w)-K_g(\bar u,\bar y)^*\Big)\quad \text{for all }w\in Y,
\]
where \(K_g(\bar u,\bar y)^*\) denotes the polar cone of \(K_g(\bar u,\bar y)\).

A key function class in the paper is that of \(C^2\)-decomposable convex functions. A convex function \(g\) is \(C^2\)-decomposable at \(\bar u\) if there exist a neighborhood \(O\subset Y\) of \(\bar u\), a finite-dimensional Hilbert space \(Z\), a \(C^2\)-smooth mapping \(\Xi:O\to Z\) with \(\Xi(\bar u)=0\), and a proper lsc sublinear function \(\vartheta:Z\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) such that
\[
 g(u)=g(\bar u)+\vartheta(\Xi(u))\quad \text{for all }u\in O.
\]
(Various additional regularity conditions, such as nondegeneracy and dual conditions, are discussed in the paper, but the open question below is about whether the above identity holds in general for \(C^2\)-decomposable \(g\).)
problem_definition_latex:
Determine whether every convex function \(g:Y\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) that is \(C^2\)-decomposable at \(\bar u\in Y\) satisfies, for each \(\bar y\in \partial g(\bar u)\), the identity
\[
 D^b(\partial g)(\bar u,\bar y)(w)=\operatorname{cl}\Big(D(\partial g)(\bar u,\bar y)(w)-K_g(\bar u,\bar y)^*\Big)\quad \text{for all }w\in Y.
\]
Equivalently: characterize whether the semi-strict graphical derivative of the subgradient mapping \(\partial g\) can always be expressed as the (closure of the) Minkowski difference between the graphical derivative \(D(\partial g)(\bar u,\bar y)\) and the polar cone \(K_g(\bar u,\bar y)^*\) when \(g\) is \(C^2\)-decomposable.

literature_review.synthesis:
The open problem from Hang--Sarabi asks whether every convex function \(g\) that is \(C^2\)-decomposable at \(\bar u\) satisfies the identity \(D^b(\partial g)(\bar u,\bar y)(w)=\operatorname{cl}(D(\partial g)(\bar u,\bar y)(w)-K_g(\bar u,\bar y)^*)\) for all \(w\) and all \(\bar y\in\partial g(\bar u)\). In the source paper this equality is proved for important subclasses (e.g., CPLQ functions and several cone/indicator examples) and is shown to propagate through a chain rule (Proposition 3.5) provided the outer sublinear function \(\vartheta\) satisfies the equality and a nondegeneracy condition holds. However, the authors explicitly note that whether (3.14) holds for general \(C^2\)-decomposable functions remains open.

The only forward-citing work provided here, "Smoothness of subgradient mappings and its applications in parametric optimization", makes substantial partial progress by developing strict proto-differentiability and strict twice epi-differentiability for reliably \(C^2\)-decomposable functions. Its relative-interior characterization (strict proto-differentiability near \((\bar u,\bar y)\) iff \(\bar y\in\operatorname{ri}\,\partial g(\bar u)\), under reliable decomposability and nondegeneracy) suggests that the semi-strict derivative \(D^b\) may coincide with the usual graphical derivative \(D\) on a large set of multipliers, which is closely aligned with the desired formula expressing \(D^b\) via \(D\) and the polar of the critical cone. The paper also provides a chain rule for second subderivatives in the reliably \(C^2\)-decomposable setting, paralleling the calculus used in the source paper.

At present, based on the provided citation data, the general equality for all convex \(C^2\)-decomposable \(g\) (without extra assumptions such as reliability/nondegeneracy and/or \(\bar y\in\operatorname{ri}\,\partial g(\bar u)\)) remains open. Promising directions include: (i) proving the identity under the relative-interior condition on \(\bar y\) (or identifying boundary-multiplier counterexamples), and (ii) extending the chain-rule approach by reducing the question to the outer sublinear \(\vartheta\) and understanding when (3.12) holds for general sublinear functions beyond polyhedral/conic cases.

sources.title: Smoothness of subgradient mappings and its applications in parametric optimization
sources.theorem_or_result: For reliably \(C^2\)-decomposable functions \(g\) (in the sense of Shapiro) satisfying a nondegeneracy condition, the paper proves a relative-interior characterization of strict proto-differentiability/strict twice epi-differentiability of \(\partial g\): in particular, if \((\bar u,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}\partial g\) and \(g\) is reliably \(C^2\)-decomposable in a neighborhood of \(\bar u\), then \(\partial g\) is strictly proto-differentiable near \((\bar u,\bar y)\) iff \(\bar y\in\operatorname{ri}\,\partial g(\bar u)\) (Theorem 5.8). The paper also derives a chain rule for second subderivatives of reliably \(C^2\)-decomposable \(g\): \[d^2 g(u,y)(w)=\langle \mu,\nabla^2\Xi(u)(w,w)\rangle + d^2\vartheta(\Xi(u),\mu)(\nabla\Xi(u)w),\] where \(g(u')=g(u)+\vartheta(\Xi(u'))\) locally and \(\mu\) is the unique multiplier (Theorem 5.4).
sources.connection: The open problem asks whether for convex \(C^2\)-decomposable \(g\) one always has the identity \(D^b(\partial g)(\bar u,\bar y)(w)=\operatorname{cl}(D(\partial g)(\bar u,\bar y)(w)-K_g(\bar u,\bar y)^*)\) for all \(w\). This paper does not state or prove that identity. Instead it studies strict proto-differentiability (defined via equality of regular tangent and paratingent cones to \(\operatorname{gph}\partial g\)) and shows that for reliably \(C^2\)-decomposable functions it is equivalent to \(\bar y\in\operatorname{ri}\partial g(\bar u)\). Since the semi-strict graphical derivative \(D^b\) is defined via an outer limit (paratingent-type) construction, strict proto-differentiability is closely related to when such ‘semi-strict’ objects coincide with the usual graphical derivative. Thus the paper provides strong partial progress/tools: it gives verifiable conditions (relative interior) under which the geometry of \(\operatorname{gph}\partial g\) is ‘strictly smooth’, which is likely relevant to establishing (or disproving) the desired formula for \(D^b\) in the \(C^2\)-decomposable setting. However, it does not resolve whether the formula holds for all \(C^2\)-decomposable convex \(g\) without extra assumptions (e.g., reliable decomposability/nondegeneracy and/or \(\bar y\in\operatorname{ri}\partial g(\bar u)\)).

title: Achieve doubly-exponential competition complexity using dynamic prices in combinatorial auctions
background_latex:
Consider a combinatorial auction with a finite set of items \,\(M\) and \,\(n\) agents arriving online in a known order \,\(1,2,\dots,n\). Each agent \,\(i\in[n]\) has a valuation function \,\(v_i:2^M\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\), drawn independently from a known distribution \,\(F_i\) over a class of valuations (e.g., XOS or submodular). An online posted-pricing policy posts item prices and agents purchase bundles that maximize their quasilinear utility.

A (possibly adaptive) pricing policy specifies, before each agent arrives, a nonnegative price \,\(p_{i,j}\ge 0\) for each currently unsold item \,\(j\in M\). Upon arrival, agent \,\(i\) observes current prices and chooses a bundle \,\(T_i\subseteq M_i\) of currently available items \,\(M_i\subseteq M\) that maximizes
\[
T_i \in \arg\max_{T\subseteq M_i}\bigl(v_i(T)-\sum_{j\in T} p_{i,j}\bigr).
\]
Ties may be broken arbitrarily. Items purchased are removed from availability.

We consider a resource-augmentation (repetition) model with \,\(k\) independent copies (“blocks”) of buyers. In block \,\(b\in[k]\), there is one copy of each agent type \,\(i\in[n]\) with valuation \,\(v_i^{(b)}\sim F_i\) independently across \,\(i\) and \,\(b\). The pricing policy observes the sequence of arriving buyers across all \,\(nk\) arrivals and may update prices after each purchase (dynamic prices). Let \,\(\mathrm{SW}_k\) denote the social welfare achieved by the policy on the \,\(k\)-block instance:
\[
\mathrm{SW}_k = \sum_{b=1}^k\sum_{i=1}^n v_i^{(b)}\bigl(T_i^{(b)}\bigr).
\]
On a single block (one copy of each agent), define the offline optimal welfare
\[
\mathrm{OPT}_1(v)=\max_{(S_1,\dots,S_n)\in\mathcal{P}(M)}\sum_{i=1}^n v_i(S_i),
\]
where \,\(\mathcal{P}(M)\) is the set of partitions of \,\(M\) into \,\(n\) (possibly empty) bundles.

For \,\(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\), the \((1-\varepsilon)\)-competition complexity of a class of pricing policies is the smallest \,\(k\) such that for every such product distribution \,\(F=F_1\times\cdots\times F_n\), there exists a policy in the class whose expected welfare on \,\(k\) blocks is at least \,\((1-\varepsilon)\) times the expected offline optimum on one block:
\[
\mathbb{E}_{v\sim F^k}[\mathrm{SW}_k]\;\ge\;(1-\varepsilon)\,\mathbb{E}_{v\sim F}[\mathrm{OPT}_1(v)].
\]

Let \,\(\mathrm{SW}_k\) denote the social welfare achieved by the policy on the \,\(k\)-block instance:
\[
\mathrm{SW}_k = \sum_{b=1}^k\sum_{i=1}^n v_i^{(b)}\bigl(T_i^{(b)}\bigr).
\]
On a single block (one copy of each agent), define the offline optimal welfare
\[
\mathrm{OPT}_1(v)=\max_{(S_1,\dots,S_n)\in\mathcal{P}(M)}\sum_{i=1}^n v_i(S_i),
\]
where \,\(\mathcal{P}(M)\) is the set of partitions of \,\(M\) into \,\(n\) (possibly empty) bundles.

For \,\(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\), the \((1-\varepsilon)\)-competition complexity of a class of pricing policies is the smallest \,\(k\) such that for every such product distribution \,\(F=F_1\times\cdots\times F_n\), there exists a policy in the class whose expected welfare on \,\(k\) blocks is at least \,\((1-\varepsilon)\) times the expected offline optimum on one block:
\[
\mathbb{E}_{v\sim F^k}[\mathrm{SW}_k]\;\ge\;(1-\varepsilon)\,\mathbb{E}_{v\sim F}[\mathrm{OPT}_1(v)].
\]

Determine whether, for submodular or XOS combinatorial auctions with independent (product) valuation distributions \,\(F=\times_{i=1}^n F_i\), there exists a class of fully dynamic posted-pricing policies whose \((1-\varepsilon)\)-competition complexity scales as 
\[
\Theta(\log\log(1/\varepsilon))
\]
(i.e., the number of blocks \,\(k\) needed to guarantee
\(\mathbb{E}_{v\sim F^k}[\mathrm{SW}_k]\ge (1-\varepsilon)\,\mathbb{E}_{v\sim F}[\mathrm{OPT}_1(v)]\)
can be taken proportional to \,\(\log\log(1/\varepsilon)\)).

An evolutionary loop could search for pricing rules that empirically achieve near-optimal ratios with small k (suggesting improved upper bounds) or for hard distributions that degrade known policy classes (suggesting separations).

literature_review.synthesis:
The source paper introduces competition complexity as a resource-augmentation lens for online allocation and pricing, and explicitly raises the combinatorial-auction analogue of the doubly-exponential convergence phenomenon known for single-item prophet inequalities. In XOS/submodular combinatorial auctions with product distributions, it proves that block-consistent posted prices (prices fixed within each block but allowed to change between blocks) achieve welfare at least \((1-2^{-k})\,\mathbb{E}[\mathrm{OPT}_1]\), yielding \((1-\varepsilon)\)-competition complexity \(O(\log(1/\varepsilon))\). It also shows that fully static prices require \(k=O(1/\varepsilon)\) blocks to reach \((1-\varepsilon)\) of \(\mathbb{E}[\mathrm{OPT}_1]\). The open question is whether allowing fully dynamic prices (updating after each buyer) can improve this to \(k=\Theta(\log\log(1/\varepsilon))\), matching the single-item block-threshold phenomenon.

The two forward-citing works provided do not resolve the combinatorial-auction question. They study prophet-inequality variants (correlations; multiple-selection) and develop techniques—especially doubly-exponentially decreasing quantile thresholds and quantile-space duality—that may be useful ingredients in a future dynamic-pricing construction. At present, there is no cited paper establishing \(\Theta(\log\log(1/\varepsilon))\) competition complexity for dynamic posted prices in XOS/submodular combinatorial auctions under product distributions, so the problem remains open.

sources.title: The competition complexity of prophet inequalities with correlations
sources.theorem_or_result:
The paper studies competition complexity for the single-item (choose-one) prophet inequality under correlated rewards. Main theorem (block arrival): Algorithm 3 achieves 
\[k(n,\varepsilon)=(1+o(1))\,(n+\log\log(1/\varepsilon))\]\u000a copies to obtain \(\mathbb{E}[\mathrm{ALG}]\ge (1-\varepsilon)\,\mathbb{E}[\max_i v_i]\) for every correlated distribution \(F\in\Delta_n\) (Theorem 3.1). For adversarial arrival, the optimal competition complexity is \(\Theta(n/\varepsilon)\) (Theorem 4.1). For pairwise independent rewards, Algorithm 5 achieves \(k(\varepsilon)=\Theta(\log\log(1/\varepsilon))\) independent of \(n\) (Theorem 5.1).
sources.connection: The open problem asks for fully dynamic posted-pricing policies in combinatorial auctions (XOS/submodular valuations) with competition complexity \(\Theta(\log\log(1/\varepsilon))\). This paper does not study combinatorial auctions or posted prices; it studies the (single-choice) prophet inequality with correlations. Its relevance is indirect: it develops a two-phase method combining an OCRS-style selection procedure with doubly-exponentially decreasing quantile thresholds to obtain \(\log\log(1/\varepsilon)\)-type dependence (in settings where such dependence is achievable). These techniques may inspire dynamic pricing constructions, but the paper neither proves nor implies the desired \(\Theta(\log\log(1/\varepsilon))\) competition complexity for XOS/submodular combinatorial auctions under product distributions.

sources.title: Competition Versus Complexity in Multiple-Selection Prophet Inequalities
sources.theorem_or_result: The paper fully characterizes, for the i.i.d. multiple-selection prophet inequality, the optimal worst-case competitive ratio achievable by single-threshold (static) algorithms when the online algorithm observes a length-m sequence and the prophet observes length-n and selects the top k values. In particular (Theorem1), for all n,m\ge k, the optimal ratio equals \(\gamma_{m,n,k}=Q_{m,k}(k/n)/k\), where \(Q_{m,k}(q)=\mathbb{E}[\min\{k,Y\}]\) for \(Y\sim\mathrm{Binomial}(m,q)\). It also derives the resulting \((1-\varepsilon)\)-competition complexity for single-thresholds: \(\beta_1(\varepsilon)=\ln(1/\varepsilon)\) and for \(k>1\), \(\ln(1/\varepsilon)/k\le \beta_k(\varepsilon)\le 1+\tfrac{2\ln(1/\varepsilon)}{k-1}+\sqrt{\tfrac{2\ln(1/\varepsilon)}{k-1}}\) (Theorem2).
sources.connection: The open problem asks for fully dynamic posted-pricing policies in combinatorial auctions with XOS/submodular valuations that achieve \(\Theta(\log\log(1/\varepsilon))\) competition complexity in the k-block (buyer replication) model. This paper studies a different setting: i.i.d. scalar-value multiple-selection prophet inequalities and the competition complexity of static single-threshold policies under extra observations (m vs n), not multi-item combinatorial valuations nor dynamic item prices. Thus it does not resolve the combinatorial-auction question. At most, it provides methodological tools (infinite-dimensional LP/duality in quantile space) and comparative intuition about how added competition can substitute for algorithmic/mechanism complexity, which might inspire analogous analyses for posted prices in auctions.

title: Remove zero-gradient error requirement in partial relative inexact Bregman proximal gradient
background_latex:
Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional Euclidean space, \(Q\subseteq E\) a closed convex set, and consider the convex composite optimization problem
\[
\min_{x\in Q}\; F(x):=P(x)+f(x),
\]
where \(P:E\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper closed convex (possibly nonsmooth) and \(f:E\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex and differentiable on \(\operatorname{int}Q\).

Let \(\phi:E\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be a proper closed strictly convex Legendre-type kernel with \(\operatorname{dom}\phi=Q\), differentiable on \(\operatorname{int}Q\). The associated Bregman distance is
\[
D_\phi(x,y):=\phi(x)-\phi(y)-\langle \nabla\phi(y),x-y\rangle.
\]
Assume a (restricted) relative smoothness condition: there exists \(L\ge 0\) and a closed convex \(X\supseteq \operatorname{dom}P\cap\operatorname{dom}\phi\) such that for all \(x\in X\cap\operatorname{int}Q\) and \(y\in X\cap Q\),
\[
f(y)\le f(x)+\langle \nabla f(x),y-x\rangle+L D_\phi(y,x).
\]

For a tolerance \(\delta\ge 0\), the \(\delta\)-subdifferential of \(P\) at \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}P\) is
\[
\partial_\delta P(\bar x):=\{d\in E: P(u)\ge P(\bar x)+\langle d,u-\bar x\rangle-\delta\ \forall u\in E\}.
\]

At iterate \(x_k\in X\cap\operatorname{int}Q\), the (exact) Bregman proximal-gradient subproblem with parameter \(\lambda>0\) is
\[
\min_{x\in Q}\; P(x)+\langle \nabla f(x_k),x-x_k\rangle+\lambda D_\phi(x,x_k).
\]
In the paper's inexact framework, one computes \(x_{k+1}\in X\cap\operatorname{int}Q\), \(\tilde x_{k+1}\in \operatorname{dom}P\cap Q\), and errors \((\Delta_k,\delta_k)\) satisfying the approximate optimality inclusion
\[
\Delta_k\in \partial_{\delta_k}P(\tilde x_{k+1})+\nabla f(x_k)+\lambda\big(\nabla\phi(x_{k+1})-\nabla\phi(x_k)\big).
\]
A partial relative-type stopping rule (relative error criterion) controls \(\delta_k\) and the two-point deviation \(D_\phi(\tilde x_{k+1},x_{k+1})\) relative to \(D_\phi(\tilde x_{k+1},x_k)\), but (as currently analyzed) imposes \(\|\Delta_k\|=0\).
problem_definition_latex:
Determine whether the partial relative-type stopping rule can be generalized to allow nonzero \(\Delta_k\) while retaining convergence guarantees for the resulting inexact Bregman proximal gradient method.

Concretely, replace the requirement \(\|\Delta_k\|=0\) in the partial relative-type stopping criterion by an admissible condition permitting \(\Delta_k\neq 0\) (for example, bounding \(\|\Delta_k\|\) in a way that is verifiable during subproblem solves), and establish convergence (e.g., convergence of objective values and/or iterates) under the same overall algorithmic framework.

literature_review.synthesis:
In Yang–Toh’s iBPGM, the partial relative stopping criterion (ReSC) is designed to make the key descent estimate (Lemma 3.1) collapse to a clean telescoping inequality by eliminating the troublesome term \(|\langle \Delta_k,\tilde x_{k+1}-x\rangle|\) in (3.7). This is why the current analysis enforces \(\|\Delta_k\|=0\) under (ReSC), while allowing \(\Delta_k\neq 0\) only under the absolute criterion (AbSC) with summable tolerances. The open problem asks for a verifiable replacement of \(\Delta_k=0\) in (ReSC) that still yields convergence under the same relative-smooth/Bregman geometry.

Among the forward citations, the closest partial progress is the 2025 iBPDCA paper, which explicitly permits \(\Delta_k\neq 0\) under relative-type stopping rules that bound a computable combination \(\|\Delta_k\|^2+|\langle\Delta_k,x_{k+1}-x_k\rangle|+\delta_k\) by a multiple of a Bregman distance. In the convex composite specialization (no concave part), this essentially provides an inexact Bregman proximal-gradient-type scheme with nonzero residuals and establishes at least subsequential stationarity; however, its strongest whole-sequence convergence requires additional assumptions (e.g., KL and summability of \(\|\Delta_k\|\)), so it does not fully settle Yang–Toh’s convex convergence guarantees under the original (ReSC) framework.

Several related-tool papers (ripALM and SpinAPG) show, in different geometries, how to control nonzero residuals via relative inequalities (often including cross terms) to preserve Fejér-type descent without requiring exact subproblem solves. The inexact FISTA-like framework with adaptive backtracking similarly demonstrates that a relative error inequality can accommodate nonzero residual vectors while retaining convergence rates, albeit in the Euclidean/Lipschitz setting. Collectively, these works suggest that the right generalization of (ReSC) will likely require a strengthened, computable inequality that couples \(\Delta_k\) to the Bregman step (and possibly a cross term \(|\langle\Delta_k,\tilde x_{k+1}-x_k\rangle|\)) so that the analogue of (3.14) can be recovered. As of the provided forward-citation set, no paper fully resolves the open problem in the precise Yang–Toh setting, so the problem appears to remain open.

sources.theorem_or_result:
The paper proposes an inexact Bregman proximal difference-of-convex algorithm (iBPDCA) for problems \(\min_{x\in Q} f(x)+P_1(x)-P_2(x)\) under a restricted \(L\)-smooth adaptable condition. At each iteration it allows a nonzero optimality residual \(\Delta_k\) and \(\delta_k\ge 0\) satisfying \(\Delta_k\in \partial_{\delta_k}P_1(x_{k+1})+
abla f(x_k)-\xi_k+\gamma_k(
abla\phi(x_{k+1})-
abla\phi(x_k))\) with \(\xi_k\in\partial P_2(x_k)\), together with relative stopping criteria (SC1) \(\|\Delta_k\|^2+|\langle\Delta_k,x_{k+1}-x_kangle|+\delta_k\le \sigma\gamma_k D_\phi(x_{k+1},x_k)\) or (SC2) \(\|\Delta_k\|^2+|\langle\Delta_k,x_{k+1}-x_kangle|+\delta_k\le \sigma\gamma_k D_\phi(x_k,x_{k-1})\). Under Assumptions A–C they prove global subsequential convergence: any cluster point of \(\{x_k\}\) is stationary (Theorem 4.1). This paper directly allows \(\Delta_k\neq 0\) and analyzes convergence under relative-type stopping rules that bound a computable combination \(\|\Delta_k\|^2+|\langle\Delta_k,x_{k+1}-x_k\rangle|+\delta_k\) by a multiple of a Bregman distance (SC1/SC2). In the convex composite special case \(P_2\equiv 0\) and convex \(f\), their iBPDCA reduces to an inexact Bregman proximal-gradient method with nonzero \(\Delta_k\) under a relative criterion, thus providing a concrete admissible replacement for \(\|\Delta_k\|=0\) and proving at least subsequential convergence. However, their strongest whole-sequence convergence requires extra conditions (KL, summable \(\|\Delta_k\|\), and eventually \(\delta_k=0\)), so it does not fully settle the open problem in the exact generality/assumption set posed there.

sources.title: Inexact FISTA-like Methods with Adaptive Backtracking
sources.theorem_or_result: For Euclidean composite minimization \(\min_x F(x)=f(x)+\varphi(x)\) with \(f\) convex \(L_f\)-smooth and \(\varphi\) proper closed convex, the paper proposes an inexact FISTA framework with adaptive backtracking (Framework 1 / Algorithm 1) based on the relative error rule with delay (RERD): find \((x_k,v_k,\varepsilon_k)\) such that \(v_k\in \partial_{\varepsilon_k}\varphi(x_k)+\tfrac{L_k}{\tau}(x_k-y_k)+\nabla f(y_k)\) and \(\|\tau v_k\|^2+2\tau\varepsilon_k L_k\le L_k((1-\tau)L_k-\alpha_k\tau)\|x_k-y_k\|^2+2\tau\delta_{k-1}L_k\). Under bounded stepsizes and standard FISTA growth conditions (Assumption 2) they prove the accelerated objective rate \(F(x_k)-F(x^*)=O(1/k^2)\) (Corollary 1) and stationarity \(s_k\in\partial_{\varepsilon_k}F(x_k)\) with \(\|s_k\|=O(1/k)\), \(\varepsilon_k=O(1/k^2)\) (Corollary 2), plus convergence of accumulation points to minimizers (Corollary 4).

sources.title: ripALM: A Relative-Type Inexact Proximal Augmented Lagrangian Method for Linearly Constrained Convex Optimization
sources.theorem_or_result:
The paper proposes ripALM, a relative-type inexact proximal augmented Lagrangian method for linearly constrained convex problems, with a verifiable relative stopping rule allowing nonzero subproblem residual \(\Delta_{k+1}\neq 0\). Specifically, at iteration \(k\), \(y_{k+1}\) approximately solves \(\min_y\, L_{\sigma_k}(y,x_k)+\tfrac{\tau_k}{2\sigma_k}\|y-y_k\|^2\) such that
\[2\,|\langle w_k-y_{k+1},\,\sigma_k\Delta_{k+1}\rangle|+\|\sigma_k\Delta_{k+1}\|^2\le \rho\big(\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|^2+\tau_k\|y_{k+1}-y_k\|^2\big),\]
where \(\Delta_{k+1}=\nabla_y L_{\sigma_k}(y_{k+1},x_k)+\tau_k\sigma_k^{-1}(y_{k+1}-y_k)\), \(\rho\in[0,1)\), and \(w_{k+1}=w_k-\sigma_k\Delta_{k+1}\). Under existence of a saddle point, \(\{x_k\}\) converges to a primal optimal solution and objective values converge (Theorem 3.1); under an error bound condition, \(\{(y_k,x_k)\}\) converges with asymptotic Q-(super)linear rate (Theorem 3.2).
sources.connection: The open problem asks to remove a zero-gradient error requirement (\(\|\Delta_k\|=0\)) in a partial relative stopping criterion for inexact Bregman proximal gradient (BPG) under relative smoothness/Bregman geometry. This paper does not analyze BPG, relative smoothness, or Bregman proximal-gradient subproblems. However, it develops and proves convergence for a genuinely relative-type inexact criterion that explicitly permits nonzero residual \(\Delta_{k+1}\neq 0\) (and even includes a cross term with an auxiliary variable \(w_k\)) without summable tolerances or correction steps. The analysis technique—controlling nonzero residuals via a relative inequality tied to successive differences and deriving Fejér-type recursions—could plausibly inspire an admissible nonzero-\(\Delta_k\) condition for the BPG setting, but no direct generalization is provided here.

sources.title: ripALM: A Relative-Type Inexact Proximal Augmented Lagrangian Method with Applications to Quadratically Regularized Optimal Transport
sources.theorem_or_result:
The paper proposes ripALM, a relative-type inexact proximal augmented Lagrangian method for linearly constrained convex problems, with a single relative tolerance parameter \(\rho\in[0,1)\). Its subproblem inexactness is measured by a residual \(\Delta_{k+1}:=\nabla_y L_{\sigma_k}(y_{k+1},x_k)+\tau_k\sigma_k^{-1}(y_{k+1}-y_k)\) and an auxiliary variable \(w_k\), and the stopping rule requires
\[
2\,|\langle w_k-y_{k+1},\,\sigma_k\Delta_{k+1}\rangle|+\|\sigma_k\Delta_{k+1}\|^2\le \rho\big(\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|^2+\tau_k\|y_{k+1}-y_k\|^2\big).
\]
Under existence of a saddle point and mild parameter conditions, Theorem 3.1 proves boundedness, \(\Delta_{k+1}\to0\), convergence of primal objective values, and convergence of \(x_k\) to a primal optimal solution; under an error bound condition, Theorem 3.2 proves convergence of \(y_k\) and asymptotic Q-(super)linear convergence of \((y_k,x_k)\).

This suggests a potential blueprint for BPG: replace the hard constraint \(\Delta_k=0\) by a relative residual inequality coupling \(\Delta_k\) with Bregman distances/step norms, possibly introducing an auxiliary sequence analogous to \(w_k\) to obtain Fejér-type descent and boundedness. Thus it does not solve the stated Bregman/relative-smoothness open problem, but it provides a closely related two-point (shadow-point) framework showing how to accommodate \(\Delta_k\neq 0\) in accelerated proximal-gradient analyses, which could inspire an admissible \(\Delta_k\)-bound in the Bregman setting.

title: Construct Hamiltonian policy-iteration paths for multi-action Markov decision processes
background_latex:
Consider a finite discounted Markov decision process (MDP) \(M=(S,A,T,R,\gamma)\) with finite state set \(S\) and action set \(A\), transition probabilities \(T:S\times A\times S\to[0,1]\) (so \(\sum_{s'\in S}T(s,a,s')=1\)), reward function \(R:S\times A\to\mathbb{R}\), and discount factor \(\gamma\in[0,1)\). A (deterministic, stationary/Markovian) policy is a map \(\pi:S\to A\). For a policy \(\pi\), its value function \(V^\pi:S\to\mathbb{R}\) is
\[
V^\pi(s)=\mathbb{E}\Big[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^t R(s_t,a_t)\Big],\quad s_0=s,\ a_t=\pi(s_t),\ s_{t+1}\sim T(s_t,a_t,\cdot).
\]
For policies \(\pi,\pi'\), write \(\pi\prec\pi'\) if \(V^\pi(s)\le V^{\pi'}(s)\) for all \(s\in S\) and \(V^\pi(s)<V^{\pi'}(s)\) for some \(s\). For a policy \(\pi\), define the action-value function \(Q^\pi(s,a)=R(s,a)+\gamma\sum_{s'\in S}T(s,a,s')V^\pi(s')\) and the gain \(\rho^\pi(s,a)=Q^\pi(s,a)-V^\pi(s)\). A policy improvement step replaces \(\pi\) by a policy \(\pi'\) that differs from \(\pi\) on a nonempty set of states, switching each such state \(s\) to an action \(a\) with \(\rho^\pi(s,a)>0\); the policy improvement theorem guarantees \(\pi\prec\pi'\).

Define the policy-improvement directed acyclic graph (PI-DAG) of \(M\) as the directed graph whose vertices are all policies \(\pi:S\to A\), with a directed edge \(\pi\to\pi'\) whenever \(\pi'\) can be obtained from \(\pi\) by one policy improvement step (switching any nonempty set of improving actions). A directed path in the PI-DAG corresponds to a possible trajectory of some policy-iteration (PI) algorithm on \(M\). A Hamiltonian path in the PI-DAG is a directed path that visits every policy exactly once; for \(|S|=n\) and \(|A|=k\), this would have length \(k^n\) (visiting all \(k^n\) policies).
problem_definition_latex: For integers \(n\ge 1\) and \(k\ge 3\), determine whether there exists a discounted MDP \(M=(S,A,T,R,\gamma)\) with \(|S|=n\) and \(|A|=k\) whose PI-DAG contains a Hamiltonian directed path, i.e., a directed path that visits all \(k^n\) deterministic stationary policies exactly once via successive policy-improvement steps.

An evolutionary loop can iteratively mutate parameters to increase achievable path length and potentially discover explicit small-instance constructions.

literature_review.synthesis:
The open problem asks whether for every \(n\ge 1\) and \(k\ge 3\) there exists a discounted MDP whose policy-improvement DAG (PI-DAG) contains a Hamiltonian directed path, i.e., a strictly improving sequence that visits all \(k^n\) deterministic stationary policies exactly once. In the source paper, Goenka et al. explicitly resolve the \(n=2\) case positively: Proposition 2 constructs, for each \(k\ge 2\), a 2-state \(k\)-action discounted MDP together with a policy-iteration switching rule whose trajectory visits all \(k^2\) policies, giving a Hamiltonian PI-DAG path in that special case.

For \(n\ge 3\) and \(k\ge 3\), the existence of Hamiltonian PI-DAG paths remains open in the material provided. The source paper emphasizes that known lower bounds for multi-action MDPs are far from \(k^n\): the best cited lower bound for \(k\ge 3\) is \(\Omega(k^{n/2})\) iterations (from earlier work), and it even arises from deterministic MDP constructions, suggesting that substantially stronger lower-bound constructions are needed in the stochastic setting. The forward-citing work titled “An improved lower bound on the length of locally-improving policy sequences in MDPs with large action sets” indicates progress on extending these lower bounds when \(k\) is large, but without its explicit bound it is unclear whether it approaches the Hamiltonian target \(k^n\) or remains exponentially smaller.

Overall, the state of the art is: Hamiltonian PI-DAG paths are known to exist for \(n=2\) and all \(k\), while for \(n\ge 3\), \(k\ge 3\) the main gap is constructing near-Hamiltonian (or Hamiltonian) monotone policy sequences under local improvement constraints. Promising directions include extending the 2-state Hamiltonian construction to 3 states (as suggested by the source paper), and leveraging large-action-set lower-bound techniques to engineer PI-DAG paths that systematically enumerate policies while maintaining strict improvement at each step.

sources.theorem_or_result:
From the title/abstract only: the paper proves an improved lower bound on the maximum possible length of a locally-improving policy sequence in discounted MDPs when the action set is large (i.e., 
\[\max_M \max_{\text{locally-improving sequences }\pi_0\prec\pi_1\prec\cdots} \; \text{length}\]
 grows at least as some explicit function of \(|S|=n\) and \(|A|=k\), improving prior bounds). The exact bound and construction are not available from the provided material.
sources.connection: The open problem asks whether, for \(n\ge 1\) and \(k\ge 3\), there exists an MDP whose policy-improvement DAG contains a Hamiltonian directed path visiting all \(k^n\) policies exactly once via improvement steps. A lower bound on the length of locally-improving policy sequences is directly relevant: any Hamiltonian path would imply a lower bound of \(k^n\). If this paper’s improved lower bound approaches \(k^n\) (or proves \(\Omega(k^n)\)), it would constitute partial progress toward existence of Hamiltonian PI paths; if it remains substantially smaller (e.g., exponential but \(<k^n\)), it still strengthens evidence about how long PI trajectories can be. However, with only title/abstract, it is not possible to tell whether the bound reaches \(k^n\) or constructs near-Hamiltonian PI-DAG paths.
